In this paper, we present a visual C++ program prototype “CadiScale”, which can be used to perform the preliminary scaling of CADI ionograms. This program also owns the capability for autoscaling the F2 and Es layer parameters. This program can be modified easily to scale other types of ionograms.

articleTitle: Barium Strontium Titanate (BST) array antenna covered with dielectric resonator superstrates for high gain and high directive antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A high gain and high directive microstrip patch antenna formed from Barium Strontium Titanate (BST) ceramics and covered with dielectric substrate has been investigated. The Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Microwave Studio is used for the simulation. We measured the gain and directivity of antennas with and without a superstrate and found that the gain of a single BST array antenna with a superstrate was enhanced by about 2 dBi of directivity and 3 dB of gain over the one without a superstrate at 2.3 GHz. The impedance bandwidths of a single patch with and without a superstrate for VSWR < 2 were in the Worldwide interoperability for Microwave Access (WiMAX) application range which is 2.3 GHz to 2.5 GHz. Compared with the BST elements array antenna with the same aperture size but without the dielectric superstrate, the performance of the antenna is improved obviously and the design is suitable for array applications for example base station.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of a novel antenna array for ultra-wideband polarization diversity applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Design concept of a compact, novel ultra-wideband (UWB) 2-element antenna array having polarization diversity function is proposed and numerically studied. The array is composed with a monopole antenna and a symmetrical dipole-slot antenna. The array is numerically studied for its return loss, element isolation, radiation patterns and gain. The array is also compared with conventional wideband polarization diversity arrays. It is observed that the element isolation can be improved to higher than 24dB over the whole operating frequency range by integrating different antenna elements together.

articleTitle: A well placement design to improve GSM/DCS and GPS antenna isolation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A well placement design to improve GSM/DCS and GPS antenna isolation is proposed. The GSM/DCS antenna comprises two branches that the longer one is for GSM900 and the shorter one is for DCS1800. The proposed main antenna has an impedance bandwidth of 104 MHz and 187 MHz respectively in GSM900 and DCS1800 bands, with VSWR of 3:1. The GPS subsidiary antenna works in L1 band (1575.5 MHz). The isolation between GSM900/DCS1800 and GPS antennas is over 21.3 dB. The more experimental results and analysis will be presented.

articleTitle: A novel Electromagnetic Bandgap Structure used in mitigating the ultra-high frequency and high frequency noise of PDS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Power/Ground plane structure is the best configuration of the modern plane power distribution system. But in the high speed circuit, the resonant modes of the P/G planes can be excited when the high speed signal changes the reference plane. Thus it brings the GBN and SSN problems. This paper presents a novel Electromagnetic Bandgap Structure which can suppress the high frequency and ultra-high frequency GBN and SSN using a special S shape slender to connect the EBG unit. The measurement results show that two stop band are obtained, one is from 0.8 GHz to 1.6 GHz and the suppression depth is -30dB, the other one is from 4.5 GHz to 30 GHz and the suppression depth is almost -30 dB. At the same time, the etched slots area of this structure is very small so it will be easy to allocate the components in the PCB.

articleTitle: Research on equivalent electromagnetic parameters of the composite media by PSO and NRW methods
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In order to achieve absorbing electromagnetic wave well, absorbing material usually is a composite media. Then equivalent electromagnetic parameters of composite medium should be reconstructed, so that optimum design of absorbing material can be achieved. This paper analyses the model foundation of composite material by FDTD method in detail. The reflection coefficient and scattering parameters of composite material are computed by FDTD. At the same time, The equivalent parameters of composite material are reconstructed by particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm and Nicolson-Ross-Weir(NRW) and using scatter parameters. Finally, the results of this two methods compared the experience method are accurate.

articleTitle: Physical mechanism of the electric field amplification in the mid-latitude ionosphere over active tectonic faults
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The issue of seismo-ionospheric anomaly is noticeable increasingly. In this paper we use a model for the generation of the electric field in the ionosphere by an external current on the Earth's surface to calculate the electric field in the ionosphere over the forthcoming earthquake preparation area. At the selected parameters the horizontal electric field in the ionosphere reaches ∼10mV/m, while the magnitude of the vertical electric field disturbance on the Earth's surface is limited by 100V/m. Then we discuss the influence of the anomalous electric field on the ionosphere characteristics. It leads to a perturbation in the critical frequency of F2 layer (foF2). We find the result is consistent with the observations.

articleTitle: Multiple aperture mapdrift algorithm combined with time-frequency analysis for moving train imaging
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A new autofocusing algorithm, i.e. multiple aperture mapdrift algorithm combined with time-frequency analysis technique is proposed and applied to moving train imaging. The train's moving information is obtained by using time-frequency analysis. An extended mapdrift algorithm, multiple aperture mapdrift, is utilized to estimate the 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order polynomial phase error, which is induced by the acceleration of the train. Experiment results show that the focusing performance of the algorithm is satisfied.

articleTitle: Design of a compact dual-band printed monopole antenna for WLAN applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A compact dual-band printed monopole antenna is presented in this article. The proposed antenna consists of a rectangular ring monopole and a T-shaped monopole for dual-band operation. The monopole antenna can excite resonances at 2.46 GHz and 5.5 GHz with impedance bandwidths of 16.7% and 24.4% respectively. The proposed antenna has an overall size of 37mm×25mm×1.6mm and can cover all the 2.4/5.2/5.8 GHz WLAN bands. Moreover, good radiation patterns and stable gains within the operating bands have been obtained. Details of experimental results are presented and discussed in this article.

articleTitle: A new modified Joint Domain Localized STAP algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The original Joint Domain Localized (JDL) Space-Time Adaptive Processing (STAP) algorithm is a kind of effective beam-Doppler domain method. However, when there are array element errors in the system, the Localized Processing Region (LPR) in the JDL algorithm must be expanded in the spatial domain in order to gain the same robustness so that the system computation load is increased significantly. In this paper, a new modified JDL algorithm is presented to solve this problem. The Moving Target Indicate (MTI) technique is applied to pre-filter the mainlobe clutter before the original JDL processing, which can reduce the clutter Degrees of Freedom (DoFs) effectively and enhance the system robustness to the array element errors. By comparison of the new modified JDL algorithm with the original JDL STAP algorithm using the numerical simulation, it is found that the proposed method can improve the system performance significantly

articleTitle: Spatial and angular domain simulation of the feed spillover in Compact Antenna Test Range
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a computational model has been introduced to evaluate the disturbance caused by the feed spillover in Compact Antenna Test Range (CATR). It is based on the far-field approximation. The total field has been computed by adding the simulated feed radiation field and the existed field of the desired plane wave. By using Fourier transform with a Kaiser window, the Plane Wave Spectrum (PWS) of the spatial field is obtained. Ripples and interference waves caused by the feed spillover can be observed in the spatial and angular domains respectively. The characteristics of the disturbance summarized from the spatial and angular domain analyses are presented. With the aid of this method, estimation and suppression of the feed spillover disturbance could be achieved in the design process of CATR.

articleTitle: Comparison of the methods to efficient generation of the impedance matrix elements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, based on the method of moments (MOM) associated with the Rao-Wilton-Glisson basis function, we apply the barycentric subdivision (BS) method and the equivalent dipole-moment (EDM) method in computing the impedance matrix elements. The bistatic radar cross sections of conductor plate and sphere computed by these two methods are compared. The numerical results are both in good agreement with that obtained by the method of moments, and the filling time of the impedance matrix is reduced considerably. And the matrix elements can be filled faster by the BS method than by the EDM method, whereas, the accuracy of the BS method is less than that of the EDM method.

articleTitle: Dual-band SRR metamaterial in the terahertz regime
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The interaction between the metamaterial composed of split-ring resonator (SRR) and the THz electromagnetic wave is investigated by the simulation. Only one resonance occur in the unit cell of the metamaterial composed of single SRR, whereas two evident resonances at different frequencies occur in the unit cell composed of two different split-ring resonators at vertical direction, which makes an expansion of the bandwidth of metamaterial become possible.

articleTitle: Scattering and emission models and simulations for lunar exploration
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents the research works on the modeling, data-image simulation and data validation for lunar exploration in both passive/active microwave remote sensing. As the first part, the works on Chinese Chang-E (CE-1) lunar program, including brightness temperature simulation (Tb) of lunar surface media, CE-1 data validation and retrieval of lunar regolith layer thickness from multi-channel CE-1 Tb data, and evaluation of global inventory of Helium-3 in lunar regolith, are reported. As the second part of this paper, scattering modeling and numerical image simulations of the randomly cratered lunar surface/subsurface structures for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery and high frequency (HF) radar range echoes are presented.

articleTitle: Modeling of radar moniter system using computer simulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This work simulates the radar monitor and a number of flying targets and their appearance on the simulated monitor. The targets are built using object oriented idea, thus a class is being built for the targets so that each target is made as an object which belong to the same class [11]. A system called Simulated Radar Monitor using hierarchical object oriented timed Coloured Petri Nets (SRMCPN) is built. This is anew development for simulating a concurrent overlayed radar monitor which is capable to detect and track multi different targets at the same time improving radar system performance and saving time and cost. This system is implemented under windows environment using Borland C++ programming language.

articleTitle: A research of Quasi optical ferrite reflection isolator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Quasi-optical isolator in the Quasi-optical system plays a role to separate the sending and receiving signals. It has important effect to the system performance. This paper focuses on the compare transmission-type with reflection-type millimeterwave quasi-optical isolator. We have done experiment at 75-110G and 175-195G to analyze the match, bandwidth, insertion loss and isolation. Although the bandwidth of the reflection-type isolator is narrower than the transmission-type isolator, the reflection-type isolator has less insertion loss, and it avoid the problem of demagnetization. The change of Magnetic Bias means polarization rotation angle can be regulated. It also reduces the precision of magnetization and thinkness of ferrite plate.

articleTitle: LTCC bandpass filter with transmission zeros using grounding inductor for RF applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper proposes a third-order bandpass filter using low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technology. The filter employs two grounding inductors, connecting the two parallel LC resonators, to provide a transmission zero in the upper stopband. A feedback capacitor between input and output is also used to generate two transmission zeros. With the help of stepped-impedance resonators (SIR's), the proposed filter has a compact size of 2.5mm×2.0mm×0.9mm. The insertion loss is less than 1.3dB from 2.40GHz to 2.50GHz in passband.

articleTitle: A Z-shaped band-notched unsymmetric monopole antenna for ultra-wideband application
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this article, a simple and printed ultra-wideband (UWB) monopole antenna with band-notched characteristic is presented. The prototype of the proposed antenna is a fan-shaped monopole. By inserting a Z-shaped slot on the radiation element, the 5.5 GHz band-notched characteristic is achieved. Moreover, good radiation patterns and gains within the operating band have been obtained. The detailed design is discussed in this article.

articleTitle: The improvement of luneburg lens antenna's analysis method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A more concise formula is gained by further analyzing the direction of ray emitted by luneburg lens in this paper. And then normalized radiation electric field pattern of luneburg lens is analyzed as well as the relation between the antenna gain and degree of beam acuity.

articleTitle: Wave height dependence of L-Band small-grazing-angle sea clutter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The representative semi-empirical sea clutter models (the GIT model and the TSC model) are not ideal applicability in littoral environments. In order to develop a really meaningful sea clutter model, relationship between sea clutter and parameters of sea conditions need to be studied. The wave height is a major influencing factor among these parameters of sea conditions. In this paper, experimental data of L-Band small-grazing-angle sea clutter were used to study the relationship between sea clutter and wave height. The parameters of relationship between wave height and sea clutter are obtained. These work play an important role in establishment of L-Band small-grazing-angle sea clutter model in littoral environment.

articleTitle: Investigation on electromagnetic scattering from the targets above and below dielectric rough surface using the fast EPILE combined with FBM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The extended Propagation-Inside-Layer Expansion (EPILE) combined with the Forward-Backward method (FBM) is applied to research the composite electromagnetic scattering from the conducting targets above and below the dielectric rough surface. The established integral equations are approved by comparing with the related theory. The accuracy and efficiency of the EPILE+FBM are compared with the method of moments (MOM). The presented algorithm is of generality for the target-rough surface composite scattering problems.

articleTitle: Investigation and design of quarter wavelength double-slot antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A new kind of method on slot antenna's miniaturization is presented in this paper in order to meet the UHF band RFID reader's miniaturization design requirements. Two quarter wavelength slots are used on slot antenna to increase resonant circuit, and then increasing the bandwidth of this antenna. In this paper, various parameters on antenna performance are analyzed particularly. Simulation and experimental results show that the antenna works in the UHF band with good gain and bandwidth characteristics.

articleTitle: FDTD analysis on microcavity sensors with metamaterials
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The mircocavity sensor using metamaterials is proposed, and the sensor operates at whispering-gallery mode (WGM). Base on finite difference time domain (FDTD) method, we calculate the quality factor and resonant frequency spectrum of the metamaterial-assisted microcavity (MAM) sensor. Results show that MAM possesses much higher quality factor than the conventional microcavity, and MAM sensor is more sensitive to the dielectric environment than the conventional microcavity sensor.

articleTitle: A novel compact antenna with 3.5/5.2/5.8 GHz triple band-notched characteristics for UWB applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The design and analysis of a novel compact fork-shaped UWB antenna with triple band-notched characteristics are presented in this paper. The measured bandwidth of the proposed antenna occupies about 8.0 GHz covering from 3.0 GHz to 11.0 GHz with triple notched bands of 3.3-3.7 GHz, 5.1-5.3 GHz, and 5.65-5.9 GHz which are achieved by embedding a spade-shaped slot and a curl slotline on the radiating patch as well as adding a separated strip on the front side of the reference UWB antenna. The proposed antenna with an overall dimension of only 24×30 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is successfully simulated, designed and measured, showing broadband matched impedance and stable radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Research of crosstalk reduction between microstrip lines based on high-speed PCBs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A new routing method is proposed to reduce the peak far-end crosstalk voltage and the crosstalk induced timing jitter of parallel microstrip lines on printed circuit boards. The stub uniformly distributed along one of parallel double microstrip lines in the proposed routing method increase the mutual capacitance without much changing the mutual inductance between the aggressor and victim lines. This reduces the difference between the capacitive and inductive couplings and hence the far-end crosstalk. The structure of parallel double microstrip lines is treated as a symmetrical network with 4 ports, simulation on the S parameters is processed. Comparison with the no guard, the serpentine guard, and the via-stitch guard shows the proposed routing method gives the smallest values in the peak far-end crosstalk voltage and has a relatively simpler structure.

articleTitle: Ionospheric tomography by using diverse data sources
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The computerized ionospheric tomography (CIT) is an under-determined, ill-posed inverse problem. The limited-angle geometry and sparse receivers lead incomplete information in measurements, which affect the precision of the CIT imaging, especially in the vertical dimension. This paper puts forward a new method by combining vertical and oblique sounding data with the total electron content (TEC) retrieved from an assumed tri-band beacon of a planned Chinese satellite for seismological studies transmitting VHF, UHF and L-band frequencies. A ground-based high-resolution ionospheric observation network (GHRION) has been built in northern China in April, 2009. Based on this ground network and the planned satellite, high-resolution ionospheric structures will be reconstructed in real time, for helping monitoring the ionospheric precursors of earthquakes over several large seismic belts in northern China. The initial of the iterative is specified by real sounding data, so it slightly deviates from the real electron density distribution and the CIT result is in high precision. The numerical simulations show that electron density images reconstructed from TEC using three-frequency technique are significantly improved after combining real observation data of the ground-based vertical and oblique ionograms. The results in this paper will help to ensure that the measurements to be made by this solid network will yield their potential.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional ray tracing in International Reference Ionosphere
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: International Reference Ionosphere and ray tracing algorithm are discussed in the paper. Three-dimensional real-time ray tracing method is illustrated In accordance with International Reference Ionosphere, ray tracing equations are resolved by Runge-Kutta method. Based on International Reference Ionosphere and ray tracing algorithm, the three-dimensional ray tracing simulation software is presented. The three-dimensional ray trace and the group path are estimated by the simulation software. The effectiveness and accuracy of the simulation results are verified by comparing with the experimental results.

articleTitle: Autoscala: A flexible automatic scaling software of ionograms suitable for space weather monitoring
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Autoscala was applied to the ionograms recorded by some ionosonde models installed in different stations. Results in terms of reliability of the autoscaled parameters are presented and briefly discussed. The flexibility of Autoscala is illustrated as a consequence of its modular structure.

articleTitle: Ionospheric effects of background density and equivalent thickness on signal scintillation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The phase screen theory has been used quite extensively in ionospheric scintillation work. But in thin phase screen model, the electron density and equivalent thickness are crucial parameters because of the nonuniformity of the background ionosphere. Based on International Reference Ionosphere (IRI), the scintillation characteristic is investigated in multiple phase screen model with different density of each screen. The ionospheric effects of electron density and equivalent thickness in thin phase screen model are numerically analyzed by comparison with multiple phase screen model. The results show that the relative error of the scintillation index with inappropriate electron density or equivalent thickness of background ionosphere in thin phase screen model may be higher than 30%.

articleTitle: Novel switch-type exploding electromagnetic pulse generator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Production and application electromagnetic Pulse is paid more attention home and aboard. A novel switch-type exploding electromagnetic pulse generator is put forward in this paper. Based on its equivalent circuit theory, mathematics model is given and calculate. By proper parameter and structure design and optimize, this model can increase the electromagnetic pulse frequency range covering and extend its operation time.

articleTitle: An integral algorithm to evaluate the electric fields associated with HVDC power transmission lines
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, numerical evaluation of ionized field quantities associated with HVDC corona is carried out using charge simulation technique and integral algorithm. And considering the surface charge of each rectangle patches and simulation charge inside the HVDC conductors as unknown variables, a set of quadratic equations are developed on the base of the potential at the boundary, the corona onset field values at the coronating conductor, and continuity of current on each patch. By Using the NGB (Globally convergent inexact Newton method) method the quadratic equations is solved, and the electric field intensity, distribution of space charges and ion current density can be obtained. Different cases of the single conductor above ground are considered, and the computed results show good agreement with available experimental data. Finally, the method is successfully applied to calculating the electric field and the ion current density of a realistic HVDC transmission line.

articleTitle: Analysis and design of dielectric zoned hollow lens antenna at W-band
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A zoned hollow ellipsoidal lens antenna fed by microstrip patches in millimeter wave is designed in this paper. The lens has 5.4λ radius and 13λ height, with a four-zone area hollowed out to reduce the weight of the antenna. The optimized antenna achieves a pencil beam for single feed operation at 77GHz, and its half power beamwidth (HPBW) for E plane and H plane are 5°. The Side Lobe Level (SLL) of the antenna is lower than −15.5dB at the frequency of 76GHz∼77.5GHz, while the RL (Return Loss) is lower than −10dB. Then, the multibeam characteristic of the lens is discussed in the paper. The radiation pattern for 7 feeds indicates a good performance in multibeam operation condition.

articleTitle: New phenomenon observed on board the ISS during a RF ionosphere modification.
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A quantitative analysis is presented of the data on modification of the ionosphere by high-power radio emission from the SURA heating experiment run on October 2, 2007 (18:40 - 19:00 UT). The Sura facility was working in the mode of periodic heating at the radio frequency (RF) of 4.30 MHz. The modulation frequency was close to the frequency of natural Alfven oscillations of plasma in the local magnetic flux tube. The effects of modification were observed onboard the Russian Segment of the International Space Station (RS ISS). The observations have provided more than 1500 images of a bright local glow, which appeared within the field of view of the TV camera as the ISS was passing close to the location of the Sura facility. The brightness of aurora reached some hundreds of kiloRayleighs. The compact bright aurora appeared North-East of the heating facility and was moving East in the image plane. The analysis of helio-geophysical conditions did not reveal any significant anomalies during the experiment. A low power of the heating RF emission and high intensity of the observed aurora suggest that the local glow wasn't due directly to HF heating of ionosphere, but rather might be caused by the particle precipitation artificially stimulated by the heating effects, such as modification of the ionosphere over the SURA heating facility, which forms the base of the magnetic flux tube (and the standing wave node) whose natural Alfven oscillations have a period close to the modulation period of the heating HF emission. The Alfven mode of the magnetic tube could be intensified during the experiment by a short (less than 1 min) and weak (amplitude of about 2 nT) pulse in the planetary geomagnetic field that occurred at 18:47:30 UT.

articleTitle: S parameters six- point method of calculating the coupling coefficient between resonators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, S parameter six-point method is presented, and the influence of feeder on the result having been considered is removed when calculating. The microwave network model of coupling resonator with feeder on each side is established. Through theoretical analysis, the expression of calculating the coefficient with the use of the corresponding resonant frequencies of the six points on the S parameter transmission coefficient amplitude and phase curves is deduced. The six-point method is given concretely with the example of card micro-strip resonators. Coefficients of the two resonators with different spacing are calculated and they are compared with experimental data, the rightness of the method being proved under the condition of strong coupling, thereby proving that it is an accurate and proper method for calculating in engineering design.

articleTitle: TDIE for the calculation of lighting induced overvoltage
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This article shows an approximate formula and TDIE method to calculate lightning induced over voltage in the time domain. First, this paper reviews the approximate formula of calculating the horizontal electric field from lightning. Compared with other methods, approximate formula has many advantages: simple and fast calculation process, small introduction error. Then, this paper derived the TDIE formula to calculate the lightning induced over voltage. This formula is compared with the FDTD method derived equations. The results show that they have the same form. The TDIE method can effectively solve the complex structure of conductor problem.

articleTitle: Low-latitude ionospheric perturbations responding to zonal disturbance electric fields
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The equatorial electric field plays an important role in low-latitude ionospheric plasma drifts and distributions at both quiet and disturbed time, which leads to complex ionospheric variability near the Equatorial Ionization Anomaly (EIA). In this study, ionospheric foF2 data from two low-latitude ionosondes and equatorial disturbance fields from an empirical model during fifty storms between 1978~1995 are picked in search of the nonlinear responses of low-latitude ionospheric perturbations to zonal disturbance electric fields. The results show that the responses exhibit remarkable differences versus season and location. This indicates that the low-latitude ionospheric variabilities caused by the disturbance electric field show deep relation to their quiet-time evolutions.

articleTitle: A sensitivity analysis of a double-layered band-pass structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The structures using periodic surfaces (here is frequency selective surface, FSS) can get band-pass characteristics, similar to a classical microwave filter. In this paper, we focus on the sensitivity analysis for the resonant frequency and bandwidth of the parameters of a double-layered band-pass structure. We use some methods and other techniques to evaluate sensitivity of the parameters in the thickness of the layers and the shape of FSS. Lastly, the results of sensitivity of parameters in resonant frequency and bandwidth indicate how sensitive the band-pass structure is to deviations from the designed values.

articleTitle: A study of a low cost Gunn oscillator with plane substrate circle cavity
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This article presented a Gunn oscillator with plane substrate circle cavity. A 2-port model is present to determine both the oscillating frequency and output circuit. This oscillator is working in its third oscillating mode which provides a output power about 15.0dBm and the phase noise about -85dB at offset 100KHz.

articleTitle: An improved unconditionally-stable FDTD method based on the split-step scheme with low dispersion
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: An improved unconditionally-stable finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method based on the split-step scheme is presented, which provides low numerical dispersion. Firstly, symmetric operator and uniform splitting are adopted to split the matrix derived from the classical Maxwell's equations into four sub-matrices. Simultaneously, two controlling parameters are introduced to decrease the numerical dispersion error. Accordingly, the time step is divided into four sub-steps. Secondly, theoretical proof of the unconditional stability is given. Thirdly, the process of obtaining the controlling parameters is shown. In addition, the error of the numerical dispersion can be decreased significantly. Finally, numerical experiments are presented to substantiate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Advanced ultraviolet-light-absorption silk fabricated by decorating with TiO2 nano-particles
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Ultraviolet radiation is always threatening our people's health, while the traditional clothes have not met the demands of resisting UV radiation. In this paper, we fabricated a new kind of silk coating with TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles. The obtained sample was characterized by SEM and XRD. Experimental UV spectra results show that this new kind of textile has an absorption peak at around 340nm with magnitude of over 65%. In this kind of textile, a majority of absorbed Ultraviolet radiation is contributed to the band-gap transition and surface Rayleigh scattering of the TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The strong combination in the interlayer of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and silk is dependent on their electrostatic interaction. This silk can be utilized as the material of clothes and sunshades, even in the military application of stealth serve.

articleTitle: Sparse reconstruction algorithm for the computerized ionospheric tomography
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A tomographic method is presented for obtaining ionospheric image with highly sparse measurements. The proposed method is based on the sparsity constraint which is applicable to general ionospheric conditions. The ionosphere electron density profile can be reconstructed with high resolution even when the TEC measurements are severely insufficient and the signal-noise ratio is rather low, while the traditional ionospheric tomography algorithms failed. Compared with the traditional ionospheric tomography method the sparsity-constraint method can provide an image with high resolution in both horizontal and vertical directions with less observation data. The algorithm is tested using simulations of ionospheric structures with actual GPS observation geometry. These simulations demonstrate the effectiveness in detecting and reconstructing ionospheric height and density fluctuations.

articleTitle: Modal analysis of Dielectric lens based patch array antenna for vehicular applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Steered Patch arrays with a dielectric lens for collimation are well suited for vehicular applications due to their small form factor and effective sealing ability. In this paper we present an accurate analytical formulation of a patch array radiating in the presence of a hemispherical Dielectric lens based on spherical modal expansion (SME) and experimentally demonstrate an increase in directive gain due to lens collimation. The analysis treats the lens as a scatterer. It utilizes techniques for radial translation and coordinate rotation of the patch array SME coefficients to align them to the phase center of the Lens. The SME coefficients of the scattered fields are then obtained by application of boundary conditions. A sample computation using this approach shows a good match with experimental results. The analysis is flexible enough to accommodate different types of small radiating apertures with different shapes of dielectric lenses that are inherently broadband.

articleTitle: The study of periodic regularity of solar activity with data analysis method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In the paper, firstly different wavelet bases are selected to denoise the sunspot activity data through the wavelet transformation, then the EMD analysis method are taken to decompose these two sets of signals, subsequently the physical IMF period of each layer are obtained by using FFT transform. Through the comparisons between the obtained results and the public time-scale of solar activity, we select two proper sets of wavelet bases. At the same time, the above method are used to dispose the AP indexes to find 6 months, 1 year and 11 years' cycle and others. Experimental results indicate that it is effective in investigating the solar periodic activity regularity and the correlation among space environmental signal data.

articleTitle: Determination of the local electron density based on millimeter wave interferometry II: Experimental operations and comparisons
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The determination method of the local electron density is shown based on millimeter wave interferometry and the electron density measuring is experimented on a cylindrical capacitively coupled plasmas (CCP) setup. Results show the excellent agreement between the radial density profiles in the central plane measured by interferometry with the proposed analysis method and by the Langmuir probe system.

articleTitle: Research on microwave vacuum drying for instant Ersi
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Instant Ersi is a popular and delicious snack in Yunnan, China. Microwave-vacuum drying (MVD) method of Ersi was studied, and compared with hot-air drying (HAD). The MVD under 1.5kW microwave power and at pressure of 65kPa can significantly reduce the drying time of Ersi by about 99% compared with HAD. Brightness of Ersi using MVD was slightly higher than that of HAD. The apparent size of dried Ersi in MVD was 0.5mm larger than by HAD. From scanning electron micrographs, the microwave-vacuum dried Ersi had more open structure and pores than the hot-air dried ones. Moreover, the maximum pore size (55.4μm) by MVD was about two times of that (24.5μm) of HAD. From rehydration test, the rehydration time of MVD was less than 3-4 min by HAD.

articleTitle: Analysis of electromagnetic pulse field distribution of effective work space of GTEM cell
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper introduces the structure of gigahertz TEM cell (GTEM cell). And the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method is used to model electromagnetic field of effective work space of GTEM cell accurately. The effect of meauring system put at the effective work space is also analyzed. This work will offer theory direction of electromagnetic field distribution of effective work space of GTEM cell.

articleTitle: Efficient analysis of eigenvalue problems using higher order tetrahedral vector elements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: 3D electromagnetic eigenvalue problems are analyzed by using H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>(curl) tetrahedral vector elements. For a dense matrix algorithm, the number of zero eigenvalues is predicted exactly and the degree of suppression of spurious modes is discussed. For a sparse matrix solver, sparsity of global matrix is analyzed, only nonzero terms are stored, and the bandwidth of the matrix is reduced by RCM reordering technology. ARPACK eigensolvers based on sparse solving techniques are also applied to large-scale eigen-solution of complex cavities.

articleTitle: Notched planar inverted-F antenna with parasitic strips for mobile multi-band applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a multi-band mobile antenna in specific for mobile terminal is come forward to support multiple communication systems. The antenna proposed herein is configured primarily by a notched planar inverted-F (PIFA) structure, an L-shaped parasitic branch element, and an inverted-L strip that is seen independently mounted on ground plane. The antenna is able to reduce antenna size by 38% compared to the traditional PIFA antenna, while the performance is good to support frequency bands covering the Universal Mobile Telecommunications System (UMTS) which stipulate spectrum from 1920MHz to 2170MHz, the Bluetooth and Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) which specify spectrum from 2400MHz to 2460MHz, and the Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) which allocate band from 5725MHz to 5850MHz in use. The far-fields of the antenna over all band of interest are verified, appearing the feature of omni-directional patterns.

articleTitle: Design of dual-frequency radome
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a five-layer sandwich radome wall, which can work at 14GHz and 94GHz simultaneously, is proposed. The transmittances of the radome wall with different frequencies and different incident angles are presented. The intersection losses of the dual-frequency radome with different scanning angles are simulated by the ray tracing method. The losses are less than 0.2dB at 14GHz and less than 1.3dB at 94GHz, which meet the design requirements of the dual-frequency radome.

articleTitle: Theoretic study of antenna scattering based on Minimum-Scattering Antennas
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The mathematical model of Minimum-Scattering Antennas is extended in this paper. From the view of energy and the equivalent circuit, the theory has been researched deeply, and the structural scattering has been divided into associated scattering and excess scattering for the first time, which make the physical process and nature clearer.

articleTitle: Anomalous enhancement of the ionospheric TEC before Haiti earthquake on 12 January 2010
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A major earthquake (M=7.3) occurred in Haiti (18.5°N, 72.5°W) at 21:53 UT on 12 January 2010. On the basis of regular GPS observations from the International GNSS service (IGS) network, Global Ionospheric Maps (GIMs) of total electron content (TEC) from 27 December 2009 to16 January 2010 were analysed. It was shown that there was a significant enhancement of TEC around the epicentre on 11 January 2010, with a maximum of ∼10TECu during 20:00–22:00UT. Taking into account of very quiet solar and geomagnetic activities during this period, we can conclude that the observed anomalous enhancement of the ionospheric TEC was likely associated with the imminent earthquake.

articleTitle: Measurement and analysis for scattering characteristics of flat plate with green camouflage paint
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A brief introduction of the measuring system and methodology of the laser scattering from target is presented in this paper. The laser scattering characteristics of the reference standard plate (PTFE) and the flat plate with green camouflage paint are measured indoor. By analyzing the measured data, we obtained the directional hemispherical reflectance and Laser Radar Cross Section (LRCS) per unit area of the reference standard plate based on the angular distribution of laser bistatic scattering intensity. The Laser Radar Cross Section per unit area of the flat plate with green camouflage paint is obtained by analyzing the data from reference-sample method measurement. Lastly, by using genetic simulated annealing algorithms, the statistic model of the laser scattering angular distribution is given.

articleTitle: Design of a broadband microstrip 180° hybrid
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The 180° hybrid is a fundamental component in microwave circuit. It's inherently a narrow-band structure. This paper presents the design and performance of a broadband microstrip 180° hybrid operating from 3 to 5 GHz. The hybrid is composed of a power divider and a marchand balun. By designing a new three coupled lines marchand balun structure instead of conventional narrowband balun, the hybrid achieves a broadband phase shifting and power splitting while maintaining perfect matching and output isolation. Simulated and measured results show that the designed 180° hybrid obtains good performances including low return loss level, low amplitude and phase difference between output ports and high isolation. Simple equations based on the scattering matrix are also presented in this paper.

articleTitle: An EMC quantitative evaluation system for airborne electronic equipment subsystem
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In traditional Aircraft EMC (electromagnetic compatibility) design process, it is difficult to evaluate the airborne electronic equipment subsystem. This paper presents a method to analyze EMC characteristics for the airborne electronic equipment subsystem, and solves the EMC quantitative evaluation problems for the airborne electronic equipment subsystem. The system mainly consisted of man-machine interface unit, knowledge acquisition unit, comprehensive database unit, scoring system unit, EMC knowledge base unit and interpreter unit. The evaluation system providing information for reference in the design stage for aircraft, provide a shortened development cycle and cost effective way.

articleTitle: Shielding effectiveness characterization of metallic enclosure with apertures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the transmission line method (TLM) is applied to calculate the shielding effectiveness (SE) of a metallic enclosure with apertures. The cases of high-order modes and 2-layer shield model are considered. The resonant frequency of the enclosure with installation of PCB is predicted by the perturbation method. Conclusions are drawn that the SE can be quickly calculated by the TLM and the SE of aperture array is higher than single one's. It is also worth noticing that a 2-layer enclosure is capable to improve the SE significantly. Also, Good agreement of the resonant frequency is obtained between simulated result by CST and calculated result by the perturbation method.

articleTitle: The design and simulation of dual-frequency circularly polarized microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A novel dual-frequency circularly polarized microstrip antenna is designed in this paper. The antenna has a structure of two microstrip board layers, and employs two circular patches which have different radius can achieve the resonance of dual-frequency, which opens a slot in the upper radiation patch in order to reduce the patch size. The antenna can work at GPS L1 band (1.575GHz) and Beidous band (2.492GHz). Applying ANSOFT HFSS software, the simulation shows that this antenna can meet the demands of the signals of satellite navigation system. Compared with the conventional dual-frequency circularly polarized microstrip antenna, the size of the antenna is reduced and the structure is compact and easy to be fabricated and has a good application prospect.

articleTitle: Research of scattering property for long anisotropic dielectric cylinders
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Utilizing the scales theory of electromagnetic theory, the anisotropic dielectric material is reconstructed into an isotropic medium. The analytic expressions of scattering field and the scattering breadth for an anisotropic material cylinder are first presented. Their validities are checked theoretically. The influences induced by the dielectric constant tensor etc. on the scattering breadth are simulated. The results show that the scatterings both in the forward direction and vertical direction to the incident direction are strong. The dielectric constant in the polarizing direction has a biggish effect on scattering field. The mechanism of results is presented.

articleTitle: WLAN bandpass filter with wide stopband using spurlines and microstrip stubs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a new microstrip open loop resonator bandpass filter (BPF) for wireless local area networks (WLAN) with wide stopband response is presented. The BPF consists of a pair of λ/2 open loop resonators and two additional resonators operating at the center frequency of 2.44 GHz. A novel resonator consisted of asymmetrical spurlines and quarter-wavelength open-circuited stubs are adopted at the input/output (I/O) feed lines to improve the stopband characteristics. The current distribution is demonstrated and analyzed. For the outband spurious respond suppression, its stopband attenuation loss is lower than -20 dB from 2.6 GHz to 10 GHz, and its insertion loss is as low as 1.05 dB. Good agreement is achieved between simulated and measured results.

articleTitle: Novel compact interdigital coupled PIFA with ceramic dielectric load for portable GPS terminals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a novel compact antenna for portable GPS terminals is presented. The size reduction of the novel compact antenna is achieved by using interdigital metal coupling and dielectric load. The dimensions of the presented antenna are 8.8*3.1*2.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Both the simulation and measurement results show that the antenna resonates at 1.575 GHz with impedance bandwidth of 100 MHz and offers a maximum total gain about 3.21 dB and a maximum RHCP gain about 0.51 dB.

articleTitle: Characterizations of electromagnetic scattering by nanoparticles using a VSIE-PFFT method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A rigorous and effective analysis of the scattering problem of nanostructures is presented using volume-surface integral equation (VSIE) formulation and precorrected-fast Fourier transform (P-FFT) method where combined conducting nanoparticles and dielectric nanostructures are considered. Both the near field intensity and the radar cross section (RCS) of nanoparticles are calculated through this method, which is validated by numerical examples.

articleTitle: Reflection and refraction of Gaussian beams on the interface of an elliptical hyperboloid
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: By matching the complex phase along the boundary, we analyze the reflection and refraction of Gaussian beams at the surface of an elliptical hyperboloid between media of different refractive indices. In our work, we extend the interface from a hyperboloid of revolution to an elliptical hyperboloid; and also expand the angle of incidence from the usual case of normal incidence to arbitrary angles of incidence. The analytical results can be expediently applied to design and compute optical or quasioptical systems, containing components with hyperboloidal structures.

articleTitle: Practical path-loss model through LOS link using short antenna at 433MHz considering FRESNEL radius
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: An empirical path-loss model derived from practical experiments through open space area with LOS link between two antennae, maximum extent to 30m, and less than 3meters antenna height, including tropical climate. Fresnel radius was practically affecting the model during different distances which has discussed. The model was successfully tested and compared with for distance measurement based on RSS technique which analyzed with the Fresnel radius. A calculator application is also generated to proceed the computations and it could automatically recognized if distance is an even Fresnel radius and recalculate the distance with consideration of Fresnel effects. Average error of distance measurement with use of this calculator was decreased by about 60%.

articleTitle: Microwave propagation in charged sand particles
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Based on the forward scattering amplitude function for charged sand particle under the Rayleigh approximation, the calculation model of microwave attenuation due to charged sand particles is given in terms of equisized distribution and exponential distribution. The attenuation is calculated and analyzed. The results show that the attenuation with charged sand is larger than without regard to charges on the sand surface, and the more concentrative the surface charges on sand particles are, the greater are the influence on microwave attenuation. The attenuation due to the sand particles following exponential distribution is greater than that due to the sand particles for the equisized distribution.

articleTitle: Novel compact circularly polarized printed ring slot antennas
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A novel design of compact printed circularly polarized (CP) square ring slot antenna fed by single microstrip line is proposed and investigated. An asymmetric structure for perturbation is introduced in the ring slot at 45° from the feed line for CP radiation. Two designs with no slit and three pairs of slits are designed. Well CP performances of the proposed antennas are achieved. For study of the proposed antenna with three pairs of slits, the center CP frequency is seen to be lowered by about 10% compared with the case without slit.

articleTitle: Determination of the local electron density based on millimeter wave interferometry I: Theoretical analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The determination method of the local electron density is analyzed based on millimeter wave interferometry and the electron density measuring is experimented on a cylindrical plasmas setup. Analyses show that the local electron density is obtained with better precision by using the proposed method than that by adopting the traditional line-average method. Moreover, this method can also be exploited to determine the electron density and its spatial distribution accurately for other plasma sources.

articleTitle: Studies on the new-typed feed network with a single variable phase shifter for wireless base antennas
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper analyzes the construction and the characteristics of the single variable phase-shifter feed network for wireless base antenna. The feed network, which is connected to a 2N-element array antenna, mainly contains a variable phase shifter, several 90°or 180°coupler hybrids, two power dividers and some fixed phase shifters. The properties of the above devices and the sensitivity of the array electrical tilt are studied in theory, which proves the feasibility of this new-typed and low cost feeding technology for wireless base antennas.

articleTitle: Optimization of synthetic aperture microwave radiometer antenna array distributed on two-dimensional grid points
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The principle of antenna array distribution of two-dimensional synthetic aperture microwave radiometer is presented. The optimization technique based on differential evolution algorithm (DE) is presented for the design of antenna array. The object function is designed by minimizing redundant array and maximizing the distance between spatial frequency coverage samples, the stochastic array distributed on two-dimensional grid points are optimized, and the optimal results are obtained. Comparing with two-dimensional regular antenna array, the results show that the optimal array can obtain more spatial frequency samples and larger spatial frequency coverage.

articleTitle: Research on phase shift characteristics of radio propagate through plasma sheath
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: As for the communication blackout problem encountered by hypersonic vehicles (HSV) due to the presence of plasma sheath. This paper first investigate the physical mechanism of plasma sheath and its interaction with radio wave briefly, and then focus on the relationship of phase shift with maximum plasma density, collision frequency, and the thickness of plasma sheath. Shift Operator FDTD algorithm was used for computation analysis, and a simple plasma sheath simulation model of HSV is also given as consistency and further study of relationship with Mach was made also. All works can be a reference for countermeasures design to against communication signal alteration when wave incident through plasma sheath.

articleTitle: Quantization expression method of electromagnetic environment outside airplane
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: It was developed a quantization method expressing complex electromagnetic environment (EME) consisting of artificial factors and natural ones outside airplane. Based on Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), the grey weight matrix was defined from evaluating target set. A calculation example of airborne EME has shown applying the proposed method with Grey Theory from qualitative method to quantitative analysis.

articleTitle: A new variable step-size LMS adaptive filtering algorithm for beamforming technology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a novel variable step-size (VS) LMS (Least Mean Square) adaptive filtering algorithm for adaptive beamforming is proposed based on the conventional VS-LMS algorithm. In the condition of low SNIR, the proposed method improves the convergence rate and steady-state error by regulating the step size coefficient. Finally, an example for beamforming technology is illustrated and its results indicate that the improved algorithm can form a deeper null in the direction of the interference compared with the VS-LMS algorithm.

articleTitle: System error analysis and pattern calibration for a planar array antennas
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A feasible system error analysis and pattern calibration method for a planar array antennas is proposed. The errors of array elements with mutual coupling effects are rigorously taken into account by using an active element pattern technique. Other statistical errors including T/R modules and beam-forming networks are described with normal distributions. In addition, the mounted errors of array elements are analyzed and the random errors with interconnecting mismatch of all parts and modules are deduced. Finally, the effects of all errors to sidelobe levels (SLLs) of array patterns are discussed, and corresponding array far-fields are calculated. A pattern search algorithm (PSA) is used to correct the existent errors of array system. Numerical results show the proposed method is valid.

articleTitle: Analysis of radiation pressure force exerted on a sphere induced by laser sheet using Debye series
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Optical trapping is of great practical importance in various fields such as physics, biology and nanofluidics or microfluidics. In order to trap and move particles efficiently, it is necessary to theoretically study the radiation pressure face (RPF) exerted on the particles firstly. The RPF exerted on a sphere induced by laser-sheet beam is analyzed using Debye series expansion (DSE). The DSE can isolate the contribution of each scattering process to RPF, and give a physical explanation of RPF. The DSE is employed to the simulation of RPF corresponding to different scattering processes (diffraction, reflection, refraction, etc.) in detail, and gives the physical mechanism of RPF. The effects of various parameters such as scattering mode p and beam position to RPF is researched.

articleTitle: A novel polarimetric FM-CW radar system for laboratory remote sensing experiments
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: With the advantage of compact, low cost and high resolution, the frequency-modulated continuous wave (FM-CW) radar equipped in airborne or unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has been well applied to small-scale remote sensing measurements. To make laboratory experiment, our Key Laboratory of Wave Scattering and Remote Sensing Information (KLWSRSI) has developed a fully polarimetric FM-CW synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system. This system can be applied to analysis and demonstration of targets scattering mechanism and polarimetric radar imaging.

articleTitle: 2.44/5.25 GHz dual-band pass filter using l/4 stepped-impedance resonators for WLAN applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A novel dual-band pass filter (DBPF) is accomplished using 1/4 stepped impedance resonators (SIRs) with low insertion loss, covering the frequency range of both 2.40~2.48 GHz and 5.15~5.35 GHz, which are the operating frequencies of IEEE 802.11 a/ g, respectively. Additionally, a new frequency transformation is applied to evolve the general design formulas of DBPF. The derived DBPF topology is then simplified with the aid of J-inverters, in which only J inverters and paralleled LC resonators corresponding to the 1/4 SIRs are involved. Finally, the filter is fabricated easily using distributed elements and the measurement is in a good agreement with the simulation.

articleTitle: A novel mixed FDTD absorbing boundary condition based on mur and PML
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The paper advanced a novel mixed FDTD absorbing boundary condition based on mur and PML, and the analysis of dispersion characteristic of coplanar waveguide (CPW) are presented. The transient propagating waveforms along the CPW, which are excited by retarded gaussian pulse, are found in the time domain. After the time-domain field distributions are obtained, frequency-domain parameters such as the characteristic impedance are calculated using Fourier transformations. The results of theoretical calculation show very good agreement with XFDTD formulation and experimental data over a wide frequency range. And the time of calculation of the FDTD method is about one fourth of XFDTD formulation. So the FDTD method based on mixed absorbing boundary condition has proved to be superior to XFDTD on calculation efficiency.

articleTitle: Impact of low marine atmospheric refractivity profiles on GPS signals' propagation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Atmospheric duct is an abnormal refraction mechanism in marine atmospheric environment, which may influence the propagation of utralshort waves and microwaves significantly. In this paper, the propagation characteristics of low-elevation Global Positioning System (GPS) signals under different troposphere environment are calculated using the parabolic equation method. The results show that the propagation of GPS signals in atmospheric duct conditions is obviously different with that of standard atmosphere condition, and the propagation power is more. The propagation characteristics of GPS signals in condition of horizontal-inhomogeneous-evaporation-duct are firstly studied, it is concluded that the propagation of GPS signals will be more complex due to the horizontal inhomogeneity of the evaporation duct, and the propagation loss may be up to tens of dB.

articleTitle: Launches of Pol-In-SAR satellite sensors and results of satellite tandem-SAR TanDEM-X
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: With the un-abating global population increase our natural resources are stressed as never before, and the global day/night monitoring of the terrestrial covers from the mesosphere to the litho-sphere becomes all the more urgent. Microwave radar sensors are ideally suited for space imaging because those are almost weather independent.

articleTitle: Design of testing method for radiation safety margins
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: An automated testing system based on a new method is presented in this paper, which is designed to implement the radiation safety margins test. System theory and composition are described, and key points of the test method design are discussed, including the correction of the results, selection of the testing frequencies, adjustment of the generator, and frequency return during test procedure. The advantages of the method are summarized. It is proved in the practical experiments that the automated testing system is efficient and reasonable.

articleTitle: A new method of matching antenna array based on coupling impedance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Based on the introduction of mutual coupling coefficient Smnqp (the coupling coefficient between the mn array unit and the qp passive patch unit), a novel method for antenna array design is proposed. By analyses the relationship between coupling Smnqp and return loss Smn (m=n), gain, coupling coefficient Smn (m≠n) between array elements, it find out, proper Smnqp will lead to the decrease of Smn,(m=n). And assuming the gain keeps constant, the Smn (m≠n) should increase according to theory. We can change the Smnqp by changing the size of passive patch. If used properly, it can improve the of antenna array. Based on this conclusion, a 3×3 rectangular array is designed. Analysis of the simulation results,we can see that the proper size of passive patch can reduce the Smn,(m=n) with the antenna gain reduce.

articleTitle: Singularity-enhanced implementation for diagonal long thin wire
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: New finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) update equations for long thin wire are presented. The axis of long thin wire is assumed to be diagonal to the Yee cell faces. Derived using the contour-path method, the new equations properly models the singular field near the long thin wire. A dramatic improvement in computed accuracy was observed when a stripline with long thin wire diagonal to the Yee cell faces in FDTD grid was analyzed using the new FDTD equations.

articleTitle: Angular distribution of LCS of retroreflector array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Ray-Tracing Method is used to calculate the effective aperture of retroreflector and retroreflector arrays with plane structure and spherical structure, on the base of which the LCS (Llaser Ccross Ssection) is calculated, and the 3D angular distributions of LCS are simulated. It proves that the retroreflector arrays can provide a wider and more homogeneous observation range.

articleTitle: A hybrid FDTD(2,4)-PSTD algorithm for Ultrawideband antenna simulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method and the pseudo-spectral time-domain (PSTD) method have been combined to apply for complex and large-scale electromagnetic problems. In applications of plate objects simulations, the different-dimension hybrid method of FDTD and PSTD was proposed. In this paper, using a high order FDTD(2,4) scheme instead of the traditional FDTD, a hybrid method of FDTD(2,4) and PSTD algorithm is proposed to improve efficiency. A Ultrawideband antenna is simulated by the proposed algorithm, and results are compared with existing methods.

articleTitle: Role of local surface plasmon modes in the extraordinary optical transmission of sub-wavelength apertures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The extraordinary optical transmission through single sub-wavelength apertures is investigated in this paper. SPP modes on the upper and lower in-plane surfaces and Local Surface Plasmon (LSP) modes propagating along the vertical hole wall are clearly distinguished. We have numerically studied the procedure of wave propagating through a single sub-wavelength hole with a 3D finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method and traced the wave vectors during the enhanced transmission using full wave analysis. It shows clear evidence that the LSP modes propagating along the hole wall is the origin of the extraordinary optical transmission of single sub-wavelength apertures, as a strong support to the previous experimental results. The role of these modes is identified by comparison of transmission properties of the sandwich-like structures made of different metallic materials. Transmission at inclined incidence for p-polarization and s-polarization are also calculated and the results can be properly explained with our view.

articleTitle: Particle swarm optimization for circular array designs in aperture synthesis radiometers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents circular array designs in aperture synthesis radiometers based on particle swarm optimization (PSO). The UV coverage of the interferometric array is analyzed, and the PSO algorithm is applied to improve the sampling efficiency of the circular array in the (u, v) plane. Benchmark examples are presented to illustrate the effectiveness of the PSO algorithm in designing circular arrays. Also, the convergence performance and comparison with other existing designs are provided.

articleTitle: A new two-dimensional millimeter wave imaging radiometer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Synthetic aperture radiometer has the potential to meet the spatial resolution requirement of passive microwave remote sensing from space. This paper introduces a prototype of two-dimensional imaging radiometer at millimeter wave (MMW) band. A G Matrix calibration approach and an iterative gradient inversion method are presented to obtain the brightness temperature image. Total least squares (TLS) image processing algorithms for improving the brightness temperature image are also presented. Experimental results show that the proposed radiometer can give brightness temperature image of natural scenes and the image processing algorithms can improve image quality of the radiometer.

articleTitle: Research expanded band for Low-profile E Shape Antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Microwave Low-profile E Shape Antenna is suitable for ultra wideband (UWB) communication system either independently or in array form. This article introduces the theory and experiment research of the UWB antenna model which can increase both of its impedance bandwidth and directional gain bandwidth. The simulation model and the test result are also presented.

articleTitle: Study on EM scattering from 1D random rough surface using hybrid FEM/BIE
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, hybrid FEM/BIE is firstly applied into scattering from conducting rough surface. Boundary integral equation (BIE) is used as the termination condition for the unbounded computation space, while the finite element method (FEM) is used to solve the governing equation in the region surrounded by the rough surface and the artificial boundary. Tapered wave incidence is employed to cancel the so called “edge effect”. Hybrid FEM/BIE formulation for generalised one dimensional conducting rough surface scattering is presented, as well as examples that evaluates its validity by comparing with MOM. Bistatic scattering coefficient of Gaussian rough surface are calculated, for TM case. Conclusions are achieved after analysing scattering from rough surface with different rms height and correlation length.

articleTitle: Predicting ionospheric storm-time fof2 using Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Using data from two ionosonde stations, Haikou and Chongqing, based on the knowledge gained from the variability of low latitude ionospheric storms, we have developed an empirical model using a new technique, Support Vector Machine, to predict the storm time F2 layer critical frequency, fof2. The model is driven by Dst, AE index and the historical data of fof2. Ionosonde data was sorted as a function of season, and the intensity of the storm, to obtain the corresponding dependencies. It indicated that the model described here can capture the low latitude storm time F2 layer variability at most times.

articleTitle: Research on time characteristic of the pulse wave propagation through the polar region ionosphere
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The pulse wave will be affected by the dispersion of the background medium and the scattering of the electron density irregularities while it propagates through the ionosphere turbulent medium. In this article, based on the time moment and the analytical solution of the two-frequency mutual coherence function which obtained by the method of the integral equation iteration. The time characteristic of the pulse signal propagates through the ionospheric media of the polar region was detailedly discussed. By using the ionospheric datum of the south pole, the average arrival time changing with the spectrum index of the irregularities, the inner scale, the outer scale and so on was also analyzed. The numerical simulation show the average arrival time is mainly dominated by the propagation items of the group velocity, and was less affected by the higher-order dispersion of the background medium and the random scattering of the irregularities.

articleTitle: Optical scattering analysis by dielectric and metallic spheres on oxidized silicon wafers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The optical scattering properties for dielectric and metallic spheres upon oxidized silicon wafers are focused on in this paper. Taking the advantage of the BV (Bobbert and Vileger) theorem, the scattering model between a wafer and the particle is established. The scattering process is analysed and the scattering coefficients are derived through expansion vector spherical harmonic function. The differential scattering cross section (DSCS) of the spheres upon the wafers is calculated and the correlation between scattering angle, size of the particle, SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> layer thickness, the distance between substrate and spheres,and DSCS are discussed in detail.

articleTitle: An improved compact power divider/combiner designed using HMSIW structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: As a low-loss, high-performance and easy-integration waveguide structure, half mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) has been widely used in the design of integrated microwave and millimeter wave circuits.
