A simplified two way 180° phase different planar power divider is first proposed in this paper. Good results in 32-36.2GHz with the amplitude unbalance of 0.5dB and 34-36GHz with the phase unmatching of 5° are achieved. Then, two types of compact power combiners using proposed power divider with the creative design of 180° phase difference are presented, the size is much smaller, and the loss of power combiners is less than 1dB at the frequency range of 32.9-35.8GHz.

articleTitle: Compact double T-shaped slots antenna with a rectangular patch for bandwidth enhancement
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A compact microstrip-line-fed double T-shaped slots antenna with a rectangular patch for bandwidth enhancement is proposed and experimentally studied. By attaching a rectangular patch to the end of the microstrip feed line, a feature of bandwidth enhancement for the antenna is achieved well. From the experimental results, the measured impedance bandwidth of the fabricated prototype can cover a wide frequency band from 2.5 to 16.7 GHz, or about 148% with the central operating frequency at around 9.6 GHz, which make it suitable for the WiMAX (2.5/3.5/5.5 GHz) and UWB (3.1-10.6 GHz) applications. In addition, good radiation performance and moderate antenna gains over the wide frequency band are obtained.

articleTitle: Relevance analysis of aircraft equipment electromagnetic compatibility
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: System vulnerability is a theory that intends to explain, analyze chain fault. This paper analyzes the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) vulnerability by the equipment topology. First, this paper delimits the concept of the EMC vulnerability system, the vulnerability source, the degree of vulnerability and so on. Second, this paper located the source of vulnerability equipment in some aircraft systems pre-design just by analyzing the vulnerability and network topology. And then, through the EMC network topology and analytic hierarchy process (AHP), this paper analyzes the relevance failure probability between airborne equipment. The algorithm could predict EMC problem by analyzing the antenna coupling, safety margin and so on. The algorithm can offered an important technical support for resolving the acute EMC problem.

articleTitle: The multi-region MOT method for transient analysis of complex conducting objects
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: An efficient hybrid method of multi-region model and marching-on-in-time (MOT) method is proposed for the transient analysis of electrically large conducting objects. In the hybrid method, the conducting target under consideration is divided by multiple regions. The numerical results demonstrate the validity and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: The observations of Kunming meteor radar and height distribution of meteor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Based on the meteor radar, one can study the radiant distribution and the time variant of meteors, investigate space debris and predict the passage time of meteor showers, and so on. By observation of the Kunming meteor radar, the observation data of meteor decay time and the ambipolar diffusion coefficient are consistent with the theories. By analyzing the 571632 meteors observed by Kunming meteor radar, the parameters of meteor are analyzed and the height distribution of meteors model has been constructed, the result predicted by this model agrees with observation data at different months. The work of the paper will be helpful to study distribution of meteor and passage time of meteor showers.

articleTitle: Study on evaporation duct model based on turbulent fluxes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Evaporation ducts are ubiquitous phenomena over the oceans, and they are responsible for much of the over-the-horizon propagation occurring with millimetre and microwave radars. The height of this duct is dependent on atmospheric variables and is a major input to microwave propagation prediction models. A theoretic method for computing the height of evaporation duct is proposed by using the parameter of turbulent fluxes. The height of the evaporation duct is given explicitly based on the evaporation duct existing in the marine surface layer's constant flux layer and the formula of refractivity gradient when evaporation appears. The modelling results and the calculated results of evaporation duct heights with the other evaporation duct model show that the method is valid.

articleTitle: Application of EMC probability entropy in system level electromagnetic compatibility study
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In order to quantitatively describe electromagnetic compatibility of complex systems like airplane, this paper introduces electromagnetic interference elements probability space, electromagnetic susceptibility elements probability space, electromagnetic interference correlated pair's information quantity and EMC probability entropy. Meanwhile, it expounds the physical meaning of the four concepts mentioned above and the relationship among them. Computation of EMC probability entropy is performed on the system level electromagnetic compatibility analysis of airborne system, the results are in fairly agreement with the actual state. Finally, this paper proposes that EMC probability entropy is an important and effective way to the quantitative study on system electromagnetic compatibility.

articleTitle: Terahertz test on low-reflection materials
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: To evaluate the transmission and reflection performances of low-reflection materials at terahertz frequencies, a simple method is employed. The test bench was constructed at G-band (170-220 GHz), which utilized harmonic multiplier and harmonic mixer. Available materials including commercial absorbing materials and common foam were tested and compared. Results indicate that these materials have practical value in terahertz experiments. At last, a quasi-optical experiment was accomplished with the low-reflection materials.

articleTitle: Analysis of UWB signal distortion in transmitting/receiving antenna systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The effects of transmitting and receiving antennas on the ultra-wideband signal waveform are different. The time domain properties of wire antenna were studied. Through the analysis of the transmitting/receiving antenna systems, formulations between feed signal and receiver's output signal were obtained. Distortion of waveform was simulated by using FDTD. Fidelities of different length antennas were also simulated. The results show the fidelity decreases with the antenna's length increasing.

articleTitle: Method of TDIE for combination problems of electromagnetic field and circuit
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Solving methods based on TDIE (time-domain integral equation) for field-circuit combination problems are studied, the main idea of which is “coupling current”. Circuit part and electromagnetic structure in the area are combined by the coupling current at the junction. Traditional current continuity equation is consummated by that result. Then TDIE and the simulation method for circuit-MNA (modified nodal analysis) is combined, and general KVL (Kirchoff's voltage law) is used to connect electric potential both at node of the circuit and at port of the electromagnetic structure. When this method is applied to solve hybrid problems of field and circuit, port model is no longer needed, and the coupling equations are solved directly. Finally, an example of transmission line is presented to testify validity of the method.

articleTitle: Negative refraction of electromagnetic waves at the interface between isotropic and anisotropic gyrotropic media
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The refraction of electromagnetic waves at the interface formed by an isotropic regular medium and a biaxially anisotropic gyrotropic medium is investigated. The existence conditions of negative refraction and the effect of the different medium parameters on the total reflection and total transmission for TE waves are discussed in different cases. It is shown that the negative refraction may occur at such interfaces. Numerical results are given to validate our theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: A study on circular polarization multi-beam antenna at Ka band
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A homogeneous dielectric spherical lens circular polarization multi-beam antenna working at millimeter-wave band is simulated. To achieve a compact, firm structure and ease of assemblage, the antenna lens and feeds are leaned against each other. The single-feed lens with different permittivity and radius is simulated. The material and radius of the lens is selected based on the foregoing simulating the tolerance between gain, sidelobe and crossover of far-field pattern. The simulation results demonstrate that the radiation patterns meet the basic requirements for the multi-beam antennas.

articleTitle: Design and measurement of corrugated surfaces for high isolation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Reducing mutual coupling between antennas of electrical equipment and system is one of the main topics in electronics design. In this paper, a standard U-shaped corrugated surface was designed and measured for improving the isolation between two antennas. The design is based on numerical method-finite element method (FEM). Detailed optimization on corrugated surface is presented. Both numerical and experimental results show that a cylindrical device with corrugated surface would have higher isolation by about 8dB than without it. This proposed corrugated surface can reduce the coupling between antennas by stopping the wave propagating on the metal surface, and it is easy to be fabricated, which is very suitable for various improving isolation applications.

articleTitle: A Doherty amplifier employing 3dB hybrid for coupling output
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this letter, a microwave Doherty amplifier using 3dB hybrid for output circuit has been analysed. In this amplifier, the novel output circuit owns some excellent performances. It provides perfect impedance matching. And what is more important, the amplifier can process high PAR signal with high efficiency for wireless telecommunication system.

articleTitle: Seasonal variation of GPSTEC at low latitude station
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Measurements of GPS STEC carried out at Hainan station, are used to derive vertical total electron content (VTEC). The ionospheric variability of TEC for different seasons is discussed; GPS TEC is compared with the NeQuick model. We have found that the diurnal variation of TEC for different seasons shows the winter anomaly and semiannual anomaly; in general the diurnal maximum is the highest in equinox months, the least in summer months; The TEC of NeQuick model underestimates the TEC during night-time and overestimates it during daytime independent of the season.

articleTitle: Calibration and remedy methods for Triple-dipole sensor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Two novel calibration and remedy methods of amplitude and phase error for Triple-dipole sensor are proposed in this paper. The computational formulas of the channel errors are derived in this paper by using the time sample data of ideal and nonideal triple-dipole sensor. Finally, simulation results verify the effectiveness of the new algorithm.

articleTitle: Novel CPW-ACPW phase compensated structure in CPW bend
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A novel CPW-ACPW (coplanar waveguide - asymmetric coplanar waveguide) phase compensated structure for CPW bend is proposed. It introduced a periodic structure composed of CPW, ACPW and CPW to ACPW tapered lines, which can suppress the odd mode excited by different phases in two slots of the bend. The proposed structure had a character of equi-impedance, which would be benefit for signal transmission, where the impedance of ACPW can be computed in the method of conformal mapping. Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations demonstrate the validity of the structure in phase compensation, improvements in frequency response proved by EM simulations.

articleTitle: The Muller scattering matrix of typical dust like particles in UV band
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The light scattering properties of particles in UV band have critical particularly applications in subsurface defects detect surface micro-roughness measure and particulate contamination automatic checkout etc. In this paper the Muller scattering matrix of typical dust like particles in UV band is presented. The rigorously null-field methods are used to calculate the scattering Muller matrix of the scatterer. The influence of refractive index, incident wave length and the structure of the aggregate particles on scattering characteristic and polarizability are analyzed.

articleTitle: Transient response analysis of helical antenna using TDIE method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the time domain integral equation (TDIE) method is presented to study scattering from helical antennas. By employing the moment method (MM) combining with marching on in time (MOT) procedure, one can easily solve the presented TDIE. Thus transient behaviours of the thin-wire antennas can be calculated. In this paper, numerical examples for helical antennas with incidence of different polarization directions are given and analysed. Also the effects of antenna height on the currents induced are considered, for both y-polarization and z-polarization incidence.

articleTitle: Design of a wide beam millimetre-wave antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper first outlines the theory of the millimetre wave circular waveguide antenna, then proposed two method which are Lens method and the method of bulging the wall of the centre circular waveguide. Based on the simulation and experimental results, summarized their advantages and disadvantages, ultimately, Proposed an effective, practical broadening millimeter wave circular waveguide antenna beamwidth method.

articleTitle: The research of using unequally spaced fast Fourier transforms algorithm to eliminate the position error of the antenna near field measurement
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Based on the extraction of spectral function in the antenna near field measurement, combined with the basic concept of the unequally spaced fast Fourier transforms algorithm, the implementation algorithm of the non-uniform near field to far field transform is deduced in the antenna near field measurement system. This method only requires to obtain the position data of measurement points, and doesn't require the probe's sampling points which locate on the uniformly rectangular grid. According to the actual measurements, the effects of the measurement points' positions or spectral domain interval of several different position error models are simulated and compared. At last, we present a conclusion that the nonuniform near field to far field transform can eliminate the position error in the antenna near field measurement effectively.

articleTitle: Study on radiation immunity countermeasure of Integrated Network Management System
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Integrated Network Management System is widely used nowadays. However, the radiated immunity capability of it is very weak. Based on this situation, the paper analyses the test principle and problems in the test. And a series of countermeasures are put forward to strengthen the radiated immunity capability of Integrated Network Management System from the signal line selection and circuit design two-pronged approach.

articleTitle: Radiated emission analysis of wires
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In order to effectively suppress the radiated interference from wires during the EMC design, it is significant to predict the strongest frequency point of radiated emission. Based on the former research, this paper simplifies the formula of differential-mode current radiation model and common-mode current radiation model, defines the concept of radiation ratio between differential-mode and common-mode, deduces the computational formulas of radiation ration between differential-mode and common-mode, and explains its meaning and purpose by examples.

articleTitle: Influence of the size distribution of particles on the MCF through fog-filled medium
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Based on the theory of Mie and pulse wave propagation in discrete random medium, using the size distribution spectrum of fog particles, the characteristics of laser pulse propagating in fog is studied under various visibility conditions. The fog particles distribution changing with the visibility is obtained, and for larger visibility, fog particles are moving towards smaller size. These results show that the distribution of the size of fog particles is influenced by the visibility. With the visibility increasing, the radiation fog droplet number density is increased slowly. The relationship of the two-frequency mutual coherence function (MCF) with the difference frequency is obtained. The amplitude and phase of MCF are compared with that considering about the average fog number density. When the visibility is about 2Km, the obtained MCF is similar to that when the average fog concentration is 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. With the visibility increasing, the phase of the MCF changes tremendously. When the transmission distance is 5Km, considering the gamma distribution of droplet size spectrum, the normalized value of the MCF changes in relationships with the difference frequency. The coherence bandwidth is close to that of the droplet number density of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> while the visibility is 2Km. When the visibility is 3Km, the coherence bandwidth is several times for that while the visibility is 1Km.

articleTitle: Transient scattering properties of dipole array with rectangular reflector
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Transient scattering properties of dipole array with reflector are analyzed in this paper by FDTD and PML methods. The scattered waveforms, patterns defined by peak-amplitude of scattered pulses, and patterns defined by scattered energy are given. In order to reduce the peak-amplitude of the scattered pulses in backward direction, the edges of the reflector are loaded with resistance. The results of array with reflector edge loaded are compared with those of array without loading.

articleTitle: Ionospheric climatology from PLP/CHAMP observations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The secular trend and seasonal variations of electron densities at 400 km altitude from 2001 to 2009 are analyzed globally using data observed by the planar Langmuir probe onboard CHAMP. The secular trend of electron densities positively correlates with that of solar radiation. At middle and high geomagnetic latitudes, the annual variations are significant and the maximum of electron densities occurs in summer. At low geomagnetic latitudes, semiannual variations are significant and two peaks occur at the equinoxes.

articleTitle: 2.3∼20.1 GHz band notched UWB monopole antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A CPW-fed compact printed monopole antenna is proposed for portable UWB devices. The semi-ellipse and rectangle structure are combined as the radiator to expand the bandwidths of antenna to 2.3∼20.1 GHz (VSWR<2), except for the two sub-bands of 3.1∼4.4 GHz for WiMAX (3.3∼3.7 GHz), the C-band satellite communication systems (3.7∼4.2 GHz), and 5.1 ∼5.9 GHz for WLAN. These notched sub-bands are obtained by etching two C-shaped (circular arc) slots on the radiating patch. The measured results are in good agreement with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: Measurement of electromagnetic pulses produced in a chemical explosion
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Electromagnetic pulses radiated in the explosion of mild linear shaped charges are measured and analyzed. Signals are captured by a monopole rod and two dipoles, and recorded by a real time analyzer and an oscilloscope. After corrected by the antenna factor and applied the Hilbert transform, waveforms of the pulses are reconstructed. It is shown by the measurements that abundant of electromagnetic pulses can be produced in a chemical explosion. For mild linear shaped charges, width of pulses is about microsecond, and the amplitude may exceed 100 V/m. The results can be referenced for the design of electromagnetic pulse protection for aerospace electronics.

articleTitle: Measurement and analysis of raindrop size distribution in Xi'an
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper introduces the raindrop size distribution measurement system, and focus on the method of processing and converting of original experiment data. The preliminary results of raindrop size distribution in Xi'an are obtained by calculating the experiment data from Jan.2010 to Aug.2010. The raindrop size distribution characteristics are compared with the M-P and Weibull spectrum model, and detail analyses are also provided. The results have important theoretical and practical value for researches of electromagnetic waves propagation, scattering effect and wireless communication system in rainfall environment.

articleTitle: The study of active mode-locking C and X microwave band repetition rate PLL-PSL system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: One of novel Phase Locked Loops (PLL) microwave controlling system used in active mode-locking Pico-second Laser (PSL) at 5∼11GHz (from C band to X band microwave band) frequency repetition rate has been present in this paper. We should call it PLL-PSL system. The complete PSL system configuration with this PLL controlling circuit was been introduced, while suitable microwave circuit structure has been used to get perfect output pulse with low phase noise and timing jitters. On the other hand, the better pulse output feature been got at optical output port. The applicability of C and X band repetition rate of this PLL-PSL system has got the confirmation under the agreement of the theoretical and experimental results.

articleTitle: A novel dual-band printed antenna with a defected ground plane for WLAN applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized dual-band printed antenna with a defected ground plane for wireless local area network (WLAN) applications is proposed. The radiating elements of the antenna consist of nesting ellipses with different major axis and a part of strip line. The antenna can achieve dual-band operation (2.4GHz and 5.2/5.8GHz). The simulation results show that the proposed antenna satisfies the requirements of WLAN 802.11b/g and 802.11a. The antenna is with the dimensions of 39.0mm×30.0mm×0.8mm. The effects of the key structure parameters on the antenna performances are also analyzed and presented. The proposed antenna is fabricated and measured. The simulated and measured results agree well with each other.

articleTitle: Investigation of resonance phenomenon in metallic cavity with aperture based on theory of diffraction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: For optimizing the layout structure of components in shell of electronic equipment, the field distribution in metallic cavity with aperture must be studied deeply, especially when the resonance phenomenon occurred. The frequency which result in resonance phenomenon was obtained by means of experiment in this paper, meanwhile the field distribution in cavity was measured at this incident frequency. The field was calculated theoretically by the Modified Fresnel-Fraunhofer's formula which based on the Fresnel-Fraunhofer's diffraction theory. The results showed that theoretical results were very similar to the experiments and could basically represent the characteristics of field distribution in cavity with aperture.

articleTitle: A printed circular disc monopole antenna with dual band-notched characteristic for UWB applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this article, a novel compact microstrip-fed slot antenna with dual band-notched characteristic is proposed. The proposed antenna consists of a circular patch and a multiple ground plane. By inserting two U-shaped slots to the circular patch and adjusting the dimensions of the slots, the antenna can reach a frequency band-width from 2.9 to 15.6 GHz for voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) <; 2 and have two notched bands from 3.38-4.08 GHz and 5.15-6.15 GHz. The vital parameters of the proposed antenna are illustrated. The prototype was constructed and studied experimentally. Good agreement is obtained between simulated and measured antenna characteristics.

articleTitle: Comparison of TEC measurements from DORIS with the NeQuick model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Doppler Orbitography and Radio positioning Integrated by Satellite(DORIS) is a high precision satellite orbit determination and ranging system based on Doppler shift measurements from dual frequency signals propagated between ground stations and a satellite. The Doppler shift measured on the 2.036GHz signal and an additional 401.25MHz is a very potential means for scientific researches on ionosphere. In this paper, global Total Electron Content(TEC) measuring principle of the DORIS system is analyzed, and an algorithm is presented to derive the space variations of TEC from the DORIS ionospheric correction data. Finally comparison of TEC latitudinal profiles are done to with the NeQuick model. And some advices on the improvement of the DORIS system are put forward for advantaging ionospheric sounding and tropospheric sounding.

articleTitle: Design of a microstrip antenna for wireless video transmission system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Wireless video transmission system obtains the widespread application in the modern society. In this paper, a novel microstrip antenna is introduced for wireless video transmission system. The work includes the design of the unit antenna, the design of the antenna array. Detailed results and conclusion are given in this paper. Simulated results show that the technical specification of the antenna satisfies the wireless video transmission system.

articleTitle: Compact LTCC balanced multicoupled line bandpass filter with enhanced stopband characteristic
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper proposes a compact balanced multicoupled line bandpass filter that is widely used in Bluetooth and wireless LAN transceiver system with enhanced stopband characteristic. The device works as a balun as well as a bandpass filter at the same time. The proposed filter is configured by using modified resonators which provide a transmission zero located at upper stopband frequency. A parallel resonator is used at input port to produce a transmission zero at the lower stopband. Thus, traditional coupled-resonator filter theory can be used to design and analyze such the device, which can obtain excellent bandpass transmission characteristic. A 2.45GHz balanced multicoupled bandpass filter with a size of 1.8mm×1.25mm×0.9mm has been implemented in a multilayered low-temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) substrate. The simulated results are that the maximum of 0.4 dB amplitude imbalance and maximum 3.2° of phase imbalance are achieved in the passband, respectively. The zeros are located in the 1.7 GHz and 4.8 GHz, provided suppressions more than 40 dB.

articleTitle: Modifying the parameters of specific attenuation model for prediction attenuation induced by rain at Ka band in Xi'an, China
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A simple and effective method for evaluating the parameters of specific attenuation model induced by rain is presented. The parameters at the frequencies from 20GHz to 50GHz are given using the specific attenuation calculated by equivalent permittivity model under the measured raindrop size distribution and the method presented in this paper, which are more applicable in Xi'an, China. The parameters given in this paper are compared with those recommended by ITU-R. And the results are discussed and analyzed. The method and the parameters are significant for more accurately estimating the attenuation by rain.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of GPR based on 3-D high-order FDTD
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The high-order finite-difference time-domain (HO-FDTD) technique is used in the simulation of ground-penetrating radar modeling in three dimensions (3-D), which can improve accuracy and reduce the error caused by numerical dispersion effectively. To absorb waves reflected from edges we implement convolutional perfectly matched layer (CPML) absorbing boundaries. It can efficiently absorb the reflections and greatly increase the computation efficiency. The surface-based reflection and cross-hole GPR modeling are simulated, and numerical results show the efficiency of the method.

articleTitle: The terminal responses of the two-wire line in cavities with multi-apertures based on topological decomposition and method of moments
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a simulation technique based on electromagnetic topology (EMT) theory is proposed for analyzing electromagnetic interference (EMI) coupling through apertures onto the two-transmission line enclosed within metallic structures. The electromagnetic interactions between apertures and the external-internal interactions were treated through topological decomposition and multi-step iterative method. Then, the load responses of the two-wire transmission line are resolved by BLT equation. The simulated results with electromagnetic interaction between apertures exhibit big gap from the results without electromagnetic interaction at frequencies under 1GHz.

articleTitle: Influence of the plasma sheath on the radiation characteristics of an antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: An aircraft reenters or flies at hypersonic speed through the atmosphere is surrounded by plasma sheath that affects on the radiation characteristics of an antenna. According to actual problems, the Navier-Stokes equations is solved using the more effective and stable AUSMPW+ scheme. The calculated electron density distribution in the sheath is concerned with the flow structure which is shown to be quite sensitive to the vehicle speed. Based on this computation module, the dependence of the attenuation coefficients on frequency is obtained by the modified WKB method. For the radiation characteristics investigation, a slot antenna covered by a plasma sheath is presented in this paper. The results showed that such a plasma sheath affects chiefly on the meridian radiation patterns, and less on the equatorial ones. Conclusions obtained are helpful for combined design of antenna on the hypersonic aircraft.

articleTitle: Composite polarimetric scattering of cuboidal target on sea surface
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Composite polarimetric scattering of cuboidal target on sea rough surface are studied in this paper. A composite dihedral corner reflector (DCR) is formed by a sea rough surface and a vertical planar face of a cuboidal target on the sea surface. The polarimetric scattering from the composite DCR is divided into three main components which are direct scattering on the sea rough surface, double scattering on the sea surface from specular reflection on the vertical planar face of the cuboid and double specular reflection on the vertical planar face from direct scattering field on the sea rough surface. A solution of dihedral polarimetric scattering between the sea surface and the planar face of the target is calculated through Kirchhoff approximation. Finally, the properties of the polarized radar cross-section (RCS) of the composite model are investigated and analyzed in different conditions.

articleTitle: Load correction in antenna time domain near field
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The basically necessary methods of load correction in antenna time domain near field measurement have been presented by this paper. In traditional frequency domain antenna near field measurement only the probe correction is needed, but in time domain near field measurement the load frequency character can result in distortions of receiving waveform. So the load correction is indispensable when waveform pattern are wanted not only in the frequency domain measuring results but also in the time domain's. If the load frequency characters have been known, the load correction can be done to get the correct waveform.

articleTitle: More practical considerations in the analysis of the shielding effectiveness
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In order to evaluate the shielding effectiveness of rectangular enclosure with rectangle aperture more exactly, we take the total effects of a printed circuit board (PCB), the loss of enclosure and multimode into account. A waveguide equivalent circuit model is established, and the analytical formulation of shielding effectiveness is derived from the equivalent circuit. The result obtained by the approach proposed is basically in agreement with that obtained by commercially available numerical tool CST. The results show that the closer the aperture to the centre of the enclosure wall is, the worse the shielding effectiveness is; the smaller the ratio of the length to the width is, the higher the shielding effectiveness is; the resonant frequency of the enclosure decreases along with the increase of the thickness of the PCB.

articleTitle: The method of determining electromagnetic parameters using SVM and open-ended rectangular waveguide
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: An electromagnetic parameter extraction method using SVM (Support Vector Machines) and open-ended rectangular waveguide, is established in this paper. A lot of S parameters, which are used to train the SVM, are calculated from the finite element models. After being trained, the SVM is used to predict the permittivity of the material using the known scattering coefficients. The simulation results show that the data predicted by SVM is satisfying.

articleTitle: The sensitivity improvement method of direct sampling microwave radiometer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: L-band direct sampling microwave radiometer (DSMR) is a novel radiometer, which trades analog complexity for digital ditto. This article analyzes the sensitivity of the DSMR and gives the mathematical expression of sensitivity of DSMR; using a method of spectral estimation to improve the sensitivity of DSMR. The experimental results show that the proposed method gives predictions in agreement with experimental results and improve the sensitivity of DSMR.

articleTitle: Analysis of microstrip antennas with left-hand stratified media
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: After deducing the spectral dyadic Green's function of left-hand stratified media(LHSM), its slow convergence characteristic is analyzed and validated. In order to calculate the spatial Green's function of LHSM accurately using discrete complex image method (DCIM), in this paper, the path of traditional DCIM is modified according to the properties of left-hand material. Some spatial Green's functions of different parameters are calculated and the numerical results are in good agreement with that obtained by direct numerical integral. So it confirms the correctness and accuracy of new DCIM. Then some microstrip antennas with left-hand stratified media are analyzed and their characteristics such as narrow mainlobe beamwidth and low elevation are obtained.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of electromagnetic pulse coupling into computer enclosure with apertures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: For thermal design and assembly reason, there inevitably exist thermal aperture arrays and slots on computer enclosure, so electromagnetic pulse will get into enclosure through these apertures, which is called “back-door coupling”. This paper simulates and computes the computer enclosure's apertures coupling effects caused by electromagnetic pulse by using Transmission Line Matrix Method (TLM). Change and distribution plots with time of the coupling electric field are analyzed. The influence of propagation direction and polarization direction on the coupling electric field in enclosure is discussed, and the strongest and weakest coupling approach is given in the paper. All of these apply quantified basis for studying electromagnetic protection and electromagnetic compatibility of computer.

articleTitle: A compact microstrip antenna by a finite U-shaped ground plane
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents a new miniaturization technology of microstrip antenna. The proposed design consists of a microstrip antenna with a U-shaped patch which is obtained by adding two downward rims at the two radiating edges of the patch and a finite U-shaped ground plane which is obtained by adding two upward rims at the edges of the finite ground plane in the direction of radiating edge. Experimental study was carried out by reducing the distance between the downward rim and the upward rim. Adding two upward rims at the finite ground plane, a significant lowering of resonant frequency is obtained with a no reduced operational gain in comparison to the antenna without adding two upward rims. With the design a resonant frequency reduction of 19.7% is obtained and the antenna gain can reach to 5.8dBi at the resonant frequency 906MHz.

articleTitle: An extended error model for the mutliport vector network analyzer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: An extended error model of n-port vector network analyzer(VNA) is proposed in this paper. With a new error term introduced at each unstimulated port, the imperfect switch effect is fully considered in the model. Especially, the model can be implemented for the VNA with 2n, even n+1 measurement channels under the no-leakage hypothesis. Via calibration procedure, the accurate S parameters of a 4-port device under test(DUT) can be obtained. Experimental verification was carried out through Agilent VNA E5071B, and good agreement is observed.

articleTitle: Detection performance of C-band radar in sea clutter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper a method of detection performance of C-band radar in sea clutter using radar equation is discussed. The compound K-distribution is employed to model sea clutter. GIT model provides the normalized clutter RCS. The results show that the detection performance does not always get worse as the range increases. This will give help to the development of maritime radar.

articleTitle: Software based DMC generation For UHF Wireless Radio propagation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents the new development technique for predicting mobile radio sitting in the case of multipath fading. Three multipath models are introduced in this study, Egli, Hata, and Lee. The results obtained in the present work involve analyzing the effects of path loss prediction models such as Okumara's-Hata model, Lee's model and Egli model on multipath propagation. The DMC contours for multipath of a Base station are constructed. The results show that the Eglli model produces greater ranges than okumara's-Hata model and Lee's model. Also DMC contours for multipath model are greater and has a higher probability of detection and higher detection ranges than Okumara's-Hata model, taking the same receiver height. This study is anew approach and development for predicting the 3D land topography and digital terrain mapping of Wireless Radio systems such as landing and Beacon systems offering time, cost and accuracy for the UHF mobile radio sitting.

articleTitle: Monopulse circular polarization radial waveguide slot array antenna at W wave band
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A novel type of monopulse circular polarization radial waveguide slot array antenna (RWSA) at W wave band with good stability, small volume and low manufacturing difficulty is designed in this paper. The antenna consists of radial waveguide slot array planar antenna, rectangular-to-radial waveguide transformer and planar sum-difference network. The properties of the antenna are realized by using genetic algorithm and available electromagnetic simulation software HFSS.

articleTitle: Reflection of Gaussian beams at the surface of an ellipsoid of revolution
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: An ellipsoid of revolution is an important focusing element. By matching the complex phase, the formulas are deduced for reflection of Gaussian beams at the surface of an ellipsoid of revolution in this paper. The analysis is extended to an arbitrary angle of incidence, and the derived results are transformed into ABCD ray matrices. By making use of these matrices, we can handily design and estimate some special quasioptical systems, including such elements as cylindrical or ellipsoidal shapes.

articleTitle: Precise analysis of IEEE 802.15.4a UWB channel model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Ultra wide band (UWB) is a promising technique in short-range low-power communication field. The auto correlation function (ACF) and cross correlation function (CCF) are helpful in capturing the statistical properties of UWB channel and getting to know the randomness of UWB channel. This paper presents a detailed and precise calculation of the expectation of the ACF and CCF of the waves that are transmitted through the IEEE 802.15.4a UWB channel. The derived results are helpful in design optimization of the UWB system. All related parameters are considered in the calculation. Furthermore, simulations in both line of sight (LOS) and non line of sight (NLOS) scenarios under different circumstances are given to validate the analytical results.

articleTitle: Analyse Multilayers or Stacked Micostrip Patch Antennas with SIE
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The surface integral equation method is applied for the electromagnetic analysis of Multilayers or Stacked Micostrip Patch Antennas. The method is based on the EFIE-PMCHW formulations with Galerkins type discretization. Boundary conditions are classified to three cases to be treated respectively. Then the linearly dependent and zero unknows on interfaces and at junctions are removed from the matrix equations. As an application of the method to practical problems, two examples are considered. The accuracy of the numerical results is confirmed by comparison with ANSOFT HFSS.

articleTitle: Calculation of Ohm loss efficiency for millimetre wave reflector antennas
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, using reflection coefficients of electromagnetic wave in metal surface, calculation formula of efficiency due to reflector antenna surface ohmic loss are derived. Ohmic loss efficiencies of different high reflectivity reflector antenna metal surface are calculated at frequencies 100~300GHz. Calculating results of ohmic loss efficiency have great benefit to the design and performance analysis of millimetre wave reflector antennas.

articleTitle: Resonator cross-coupled bandpass filters with spurious suppression
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A direct and cross cascade of coupled microwave filter using an open loop resonator are proposed. This paper presents theirs efficiency are enhancement by employing the quadruply-step impedance transmission lines compensated parallel-coupled line. The spurious responses are occurred. Simple empirical models are designed and fabricated to solve this problems, the directivity enhanced parallel-coupler should be employed. The measured results are in good agreement with the simulated prediction and the operating frequency is 0.9GHz.

articleTitle: The applications of multiple phase-screen technique in ionospheric scintillation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Understanding the effects of propagation of radio wave through ionospheric irregularities is critical in the design of transionospheric link. In this paper, some results of scintillation simulations based on the multiple phase-screen (MPS) technique is presented. The results include the fluctuation of amplitude and phase of received signal, the calculation of S4 and sigmaphi index, and the distortion of wideband pulse shape. It can be seen that the MPS technique is very convenient in the modelling of transionospheric scintillation channel.

articleTitle: The optimization of contoured beam reflector antenna based on DEGL
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The application of Differential Evolution algorithm with Global and Local neighborhoods (DEGL) in the shaping of the reflector antenna is presented. A single offset circular reflector antenna with a single feed is shaped in order to produce a contoured beam that covers the China territory in Ku band. Physical optics (PO) and Physical Theory of Diffraction (PTD) are employed to accurately analysis the antenna. The optimization results, which prove that DEGL is efficient and powerful, are validated by the commercial software GRASP9.3.01.

articleTitle: An efficient method for analysing radiation pattern of wide scanning phased array antenna enclosed by dielectric radomes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents an efficient method for analyzing the performance of dielectric radomes illuminated by phased array antennas with wide scanning angles using volume integral equation based on the method of moment (VIE-MoM). A concise relationship between the unknown electric density flux of VIE-MoM and the scanning angle is derived and applied to avoid repeatedly solving the large matrix equation generated by VIE-MoM. Numerical results demonstrate that the computational efficiency can be significantly improved by the proposed approach for the wide scanning problems.

articleTitle: Research on quasi-optics and feed antenna for Millimeter wave imaging system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The quasi-optics sub-system of Millimeter-wave focal plane arrays imaging system includes the design of system parameters, multi-beam design of focusing element and design of feed antenna. Design of focusing element decides the spatial resolution and the maximum field of view of the system. The design and arrangement of the feed antenna related to the overflow efficiency and the spatial sampling rate of the system. In this paper, fundamental mode Gaussian beam method is taken to design quasi-optics, and focusing lens antenna is designed with the principle of optical path difference of feed sources on optical axis. In this paper also proposed a new kind of dielectric rod antenna with new structure as the feed source to the lens. The simulation and measurement show that the multi-beam lens antenna has a better wide-angle scanning feather. The feed antenna has broader wave band, lower side lobe, lower mutual coupling, lower cross polarization, and the gain of it can be changed by changing its length but not the section area. It is easier to form a close feed array which can realize an effective exposure to the lens or the reflector antenna with less overflow loss.

articleTitle: Compact microstrip stepped impedance dual-band bandpass filter with high selectivity
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A compact tri-section stepped impedance dual-band bandpass filter is presented. The tri-section stepped impedance resonator (SIR) is adopted to result in two tunable passbands. It offers further reduced overall size than conventional two-section SIR. The locations of the two passbands can be adjusted by changing the ratio of impedance. The measured results exhibit a good dual-band filtering performance with return losses higher than −17dB. Two transmission zeros ensure a high out-of-band rejection. With the new structure, the filter has not only high selectivity but also compact size.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband pulse generator with cascode impulse shaping circuit
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Ultra-wideband (UWB) pulse generator circuit is said to be the heart of any UWB systems. It is the fundamental circuit for application and development of UWB technology. This paper presents an UWB pulse generator with cascode transistors operating as a pulse shaping circuit to generate Gaussian pulses. In this work, the UWB pulse generator consists of three parts: an edge triggered driver, an edge sharpener SRD, and a cascode for impulse shaping. The proposed circuit allows the generator to create short and high amplitude Gaussian-like pulses at low-cost. Our measured UWB pulse was 1.0 ns pulse with 2.8 Vpeak.

articleTitle: Planar UWB antenna with notched band employing embedded open stub
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A new frequency notched ultra-wideband microstrip antenna with embedded open stub is proposed. The antenna consists of a conventional U shape radiation patch and modified ground plane. By introducing an embedded open-circuit stub, frequency notched band is obtained. The operation bandwidth of the antenna is 2.35–11.2 GHz, in which a frequency notched band of 5.3 – 5.9 GHz has been achieved. Simulation results are confirmed via experiment, showing good ultra-wideband performance and making it advantageous for high speed wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Human body impedance model and human age dependence of dielectric properties
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A cylinder model of human body bio-impedance was proposed and analyzed with equivalent circuits and simulation method, so as to get some hints for possible medical diagnosis and physiology information. Neighboring effect exist for subject body placed in transverse electromagnetic (TEM) chamber. Description was given on frequency range for in-body ultra-wide band communication channel, and on correlation between people age and electric parameters of permeability, conductivity in skin and muscles of human body.

articleTitle: Design of a directional ultra-wideband planar antenna array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The design of a directional ultra-wideband printed circular monopole antenna array operating in 3.1-10.6 GHz is proposed in this paper. The two elements of the array are fed by a broadband T-junction power divider. The antenna's occupied bandwidth of the return loss on a -10 dB level is 7.98 GHz which is from 2.74 GHz to 11.65 GHz where the octave band is 4.25. The gains are 5.25 dB at 3 GHz, 7.56 dB at 6 GHz and 8.62 dB at 9 GHz, respectively. The final size of this antenna is 28.4×67 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and the thickness is 1 mm. The proposed antenna array could be easily integrated and apply to the directional long-distance terrestrial UWB communication systems effectively.

articleTitle: A compact CPW-fed elliptical-slot UWB antenna with dual band-notched features
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A compact CPW-fed elliptical-slot ultra wide band (UWB) antenna with dual band-notched features has been proposed. The two band-notches are designed to avoid possible interference with the existing 3.3–3.7GHz band for IEEE802.16 WiMAX, 3.7–4.2GHz band for satellite communication and 5–6GHz for IEEE802.11a WLAN and HIPERLAN/2 WLAN. An elliptical slot is cut on the ground plane and a similar stub is embedded in it as the radiation element. The dual band-notched features are obtained by moving two similar unclosed elliptical ring slots. The simulated and measured results illustrate the proposed antenna has good broadband impedance matching, stable gain and consistent radiation patterns.

articleTitle: A Quasi-Yagi microstrip antenna with simplified feeding structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a Quasi-Yagi antenna with a simplified feeding network is proposed. The impedance bandwidth, radiation patterns and gain of the proposed antenna are studied by the Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method. The simulated and measured results show that the accomplished bandwidth of the antenna can cover a frequency range from 4.64 GHz to 6.25 GHz, which involves the two WLAN bands of 5.15 GHz to 5.25 GHz and 5.75 GHz to 5.85 GHz. Within the frequency band, the radiation characteristic of the antenna exhibits a good performance, and the maximum gain is about 7.2 dB. The antenna is easy to integrate with the microwave circuits and other solid devices.

articleTitle: Study and design of a broadband monopole antenna using non-Foster circuits
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The possibility of using non-Foster circuit to expand the bandwidth of a monopole antenna is investigated theoretically. Beginning with an inductor-loaded monopole antenna resonating at different frequencies by changing the value of the loaded inductor, we show that a frequency-dependent inductor is needed to enhance the bandwidth of the monopole antenna. This enlightens us to use a non-Foster reactive circuit to realize the frequency-dependent inductor. Based on the above studies, simulated results demonstrate that the input reactance of the non- Foster loaded antenna becomes stable and approaches zero, which favours the impedance matching and extends the bandwidth to a certain extent. Finally, a passive (Foster) matching circuit is designed to improve the bandwidth further.

articleTitle: A pilot emergency communication system based on IP and airship
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The problems facing the communication for emergency response were recently highlighted by frequent disasters. When stricken by a catastrophic natural or man-made disaster, terrestrial networks are severely destroyed, and satellite communication networks are deficient in bandwidth. Therefore, the communication systems are urgently needed in emergency response. In this paper, we extend the previous works about emergency communication for electric power system based on airship, and present a pilot emergency communication system based on IP and airship. The feasibility of the emergency communication system based on IP and airship are confirmed by experiment in Qujing City of Yunnan Province, China.

articleTitle: Compact broad-band annular ring antenna for global navigation satellite systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A compact circularly polarized annular ring antenna is proposed for global navigation satellite systems (GNSS). The antenna is excited by two L-probes connected to the 90± power divider printed on the back. The high impedance of the annular ring working at TM <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode is transformed to low values by the L-probes. The antenna has a 44.2% 10-dB return loss bandwidth and a 37.8% 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth, respectively, due to the L-probes and the power divider. The gain bandwidth of the antenna is sufficiently enough to cover the bands of COMPASS, Galileo, GPS and GLONASS systems around 1.575 GHz.

articleTitle: A novel dual-sleeve antenna unrelated with ground
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This correspondence presents a dual sleeve antenna which is unrelated with ground plane for broadband applications. The proposed omnidirectional antenna, which works from 400MHz to 900MHz in frequency, applies choking technique to eliminate the effect of ground plane. Working principle, design proposals as well as some key points during design procedure are addressed in this article as well. The antenna is simulated and fabricated; the measured characters show reasonable agreement with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: Prediction of crosstalk effects in future multiwall carbon nanotube (MWCNT) interconnects
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the crosstalk effects in future very large-scale integration (VLSI) interconnects based on multiwall carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) are investigated with the equivalent single conductor (ESC) model and finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) solution of transmission line equations. The worst-case time delay and the peak crosstalk voltage on the victim wire of MWCNT interconnects are derived and compared to the copper wire counterparts for the intermediate interconnects with lengths of 10 ~ 1000 μm at 22 nm and 14 nm technology nodes. The numerical results represent that the advantages of time delay for MWCNT interconnects are more obvious for longer wire lengths and smaller technology nodes. While MWCNT interconnects have little improvement in the crosstalk-induced noises compared to their Cu counterparts.

articleTitle: Simulation of electromagnetic interference from GSM wireless phones in transport airplanes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The electromagnetic environment of a GSM wireless network inside a transport airplane is investigated to provide quantification of the electromagnetic interference (EMI) threat. An Airbus A319 with an excited 800MHz dipole inside its cabin is modelled in commercial electromagnetic simulation software EMPIRE-XCcel. The received power along window seats is calculated and validated using experimental data. Thereafter, The validated method is applied to the investigation of a GSM cellular network inside a larger aircraft. Simulation results show that the peak of coupled E-field strength in cockpit and cargo bay do not exceed the radiated susceptibility test levels in RTCA/DO-160F. This means the likelihood of interference with onboard devices is low. The research method can be applied to the EMI evaluation of various airplane types and other electrically large and complex structure.

articleTitle: Polarization-insensitive planar left-handed metamaterials
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new kind of four-fold symmetric planar left-handed metamaterial (LHM) which consists of a cross and a ring. The results demonstrate that the left-handed metamaterial has a pass band at around 12.79GHz. Negative refractive index realizes with both negative permittivity and negative permeability over the same frequency. Also S-parameter retrieval method is used to extract effective permittivity, permeability and refractive index. Refractive index below zero extends from frequency of 12.43GHz to 13.64GHz. At last, transmission properties with different polarizations of incident EM waves are discussed which verify the polarization-insensitive left-handed metamaterial.

articleTitle: Design and performance analysis of the rectangular spiral microstrip antenna and its array configuration
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper a rectangular spiral microstrip antenna and its array configuration are designed and their performances are analyzed in term of return loss response and radiation pattern. Microstrip antenna design equations are introduced and the proposed antenna is simulated by using SONNET version V12.56 simulator. The resonant frequency of array antenna is 10.6 GHz. The main feature of this spiral antenna is that it can be designed for the operating frequency at any range with higher radiation efficiency compared to other conventional microstrip antennas and its array network configuration provides higher radiation performance in term of directive gain and maximum radiation.

articleTitle: Analysis of the effect of slot resolution on the simulating precision of thin-slot coupling with parallel implementation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents a new method with parallel FDTD algorithm based on MPI library to analyze thin-slot coupling, which often leads to huge computation. It is demonstrated that the adopted parallel strategy is feasible by comparing the results of serial FDTD computation with that of the proposed method. The high efficiency of this method is also proved. Comparison of the field components given by different slot resolutions indicates that the simulating error is huge when just several grids are used to model the slot and numerical convergence has been achieved with 15 cells/slot width.

articleTitle: The humidity retrievals using BP neural network algorithm based on mexihat or morlet wavelet function in clear-sky
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The paper presents three algorithms to retrieve the humidity profiles from the observing datasets of FENGYUN-3A (FY-3A) satellite microwave humidity sensor. Compared to widely used algorithm-BP artificial neural network (BP-ANN), the algorithms of ANN based on morelet and mexihat function can avoid the conditions of easily getting stuck in local minima and reaching convergence with long time. Especially, the BP-ANN with mexihat function can decrease the training time and improve the humidity retrievals.

articleTitle: Open loop resonator bandpass filters design using the parallel coupled line technique
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper describes the design of open loop ring resonator based on the parallel coupled line technique, enhances efficiency by using the quadruply-step impedance transmission line. The proposed resonator is consisted of three sections quarter wavelength coupler and each of sections has the folded open-stubs with the electrical length and characteristic impedance λ/8 and Z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> connected in the end of each ports. The spurious response at 2f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> and 3f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> are appeared. The directivity enhanced parallel-coupler should be employed to solve this problem. The experimental results and designs of all type are 0.9 GHz to implement bandpass filters. There were evidently shown the second spurious response suppression improvement and shifted third spurious response to higher frequency. Both the theoretical and experimental performance is presented.

articleTitle: A wideband aperture-coupled microstrip patch antenna with backed cavity of dielectric
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A novel wideband aperture-coupled patch antenna is presented in this paper. The antenna has a cavity of dielectric backed configuration, which can avoid the back radiation of the aperture and suppress the excitation and propagation of a parallel plate mode between the up and below ground plane. The antenna is fed by an inhomogeneous stripline, which is convenient for the vertical connection between the feed-line and the coax probe. The cavity with reasonable size contributes to excite the mutual resonance between the aperture and patch, which afford a broadband solution. The simulated results show the 10dB-bandwidth exceeds 40%, and the cross-polarization of E plane and H plane are all lower than −40dB. Furthermore, the antenna has a simple configuration, and is benefit for being integrated with other RF and control devices through via holes.

articleTitle: The starting thrust simulation of a Tubular linear motor on the base of finite element analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: As a pushing motor, a Tubular linear motor (TLM) can provide high instantaneous starting thrust. According to the characteristics of the pushing motor, this paper studies the thrust characteristics of tubular linear motor and analyses the starting thrust characteristics in different conditions including: materials of the secondary, length of air-gap and width of the primary tooth. The analysis results provide a foundation for the optimum design of TLM for pushing unit.

articleTitle: Study on acceleration technique for two-dimensional FDTD algorithm based on GPU
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The Parallel finite difference time domain (FDTD) algorithm is an important method to 1 enhance the speed in multiple data FDTD operation. The improvement of graphics processing unit (GPU) performance, especially the emergence of Computer Unit Device Architecture (CUDA), offers parallel FDTD method an efficient and simple solution. First of all, this paper explains parallel FDTD method and CUDA in detail, and then elaborates the parallel speedup principle of two-dimensional FDTD algorithm by use of GPU on the CUDA platform. At last, this paper analyzes computing time of the FDTD algorithm on two different CPUs and GPUs. The result shows the consistency of the results between serial and parallel algorithms, and observably speedup is obtained compared with traditional PC computation by use of GPU.

articleTitle: The error analysis and improvement of microwave resonant cavity method in steam turbine exhaust wetness measurement
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper analyses the theory of wet measurement using microwave cavity and designs cylindrical resonator sensor with coaxial-cylindrical waveguide circuit grid divider which works with TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">011</sub> mode and has higher quality factor. Rectangular waveguide is adopted to excite and couple with cylindrical resonator sensor at the end of the waveguide through small hole. The result shows that the resonator humidity sensor meets the practical requirements of humidity measurement system. This paper analyses the uncertainty of the theory formula for measuring the humidity of wet steam on-line. Based on perturbation theory, a formula for engineering is deduced according to the theory that the energy storage of electric field equals the energy storage of magnetic field when resonance is happened. This paper analyses and compares the errors caused by three kind of formula, and the theoretical uncertainty comparison curve is given. The result shows that the measurement accuracy can be increased more than three times with the formula presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Advances in numerical simulation of composite scattering from target above rough surface
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Study of radar echoes from the targets in environmental clutters has been of great interest in many applications. In this paper, research works on theoretical modeling and numerical simulations of composite electromagnetic scattering from target and rough surface are briefly reported. It includes GFBM/SAA, Hybrid KA-MoM, FEM with CMPL-DDM-TLQST, FDTD, and BART, developed in this Lab during recent years. GFBM/SAA: generalized forward backward method with spectral accelerate algorithm Hybrid KA-MoM: hybrid analytic Kirchhoff approximation and numerical method of moment FEM with CMPL, DDM and TLQST: finite element method with conformal perfectly matched layer, domain decomposition method, and two level quasistationary algorithm FDTD: finite difference time domain BART: bidirectional analytic ray tracing.

Author Keywords: GFBM/SAA: generalized forward backward method with
Hybrid KA-MoM: hybrid analytic Kirchhoff approximation and numerical method of moment
FEM with CMPL, DDM and TLQST: finite element

articleTitle: Inverse method for designing external cloak based on Laplace's equation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The external cloak is a special device that can make an object outside the cloaking shell invisible. In this paper, the inverse method based on numerical solution of Laplace's equation is applied to design arbitrary shape external cloak, without any knowledge of the coordinate transformation. The performance of the cloak is verified by full-wave simulation. The design method is extended to three dimensional case, which greatly enhances the applicability of external cloak.

articleTitle: Highly reliable & adaptive SMART phased array antenna with gain adjustment & beam forming capabilities for space applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper discusses design & measurement techniques for highly reliable, adaptive & SMART electronically steerable phased array antenna with gain adjustment & beam forming capability for space applications. Complexity of feeding network for phased array antenna has been reduced by many folds with the use of 16 independently coaxial fed circularly polarized truncated corner patch elements in sequentially rotated configuration providing an excellent axial ratio of <;0.1 dB for entire array highly recommended for satellite communication. Independent element digital control enables the options for beam steering through phase shifters, gain adjustment, & combinations of multiple adaptive beam generation discussed in detail. The chains from transmitter to antenna for beam steering network have also been discussed. Reliability analysis through antenna measurements show degradation in gain is less due to failure of elements as compared to other antennas. Phased array antenna has been simulated & optimized on Ansoft HFSS v11.

articleTitle: High resolution radar imaging based on compressed sensing using sparse stepped-frequency signal
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In the face of sparse aperture data imaging, a method for high resolution radar imaging based on compressed sensing using sparse stepped-frequency signal is proposed in this letter. In the signal stretching process, high resolution target echo can be acquired through second sample for the coarse-resolution range profile. Based on the sparsity of the signal in the spectrogram, we can construct a reasonable partial fourier sparse basis matrix to realize the sparsity of radar data. Then, the high-resolution range profile information is recovered by using the Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) algorithm, and the high resolution target imaging can be gained whose target sidelobe is suppressed efficiently. Finally, the results with simulation data validate the feasibility and superiority of the approach.

articleTitle: Antarctic SLF/ELF radio atmospheric noise measure and research in China
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: It is the first time that the Antarctic super low frequency (SLF) and extremely low frequency (ELF) radio atmospheric noise has been measured in China. The time domain profile and the frequency domain profile of the data have been gained by analyzing and processing the measured data, and the change characteristic of the radio atmospheric noise has been discussed along the day, night and the frequency. The analysis of the measured data shows that the value of the radio atmospheric noise is very low in South Pole. It can reveal the real radio atmospheric noise because it avoids effectively the industry and the artificial electromagnetic interference. Moreover, the characteristic of Schumann resonance is very obvious.

articleTitle: ISAR imaging analysis of Bistatic FMCW radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper studies the basic issue of Bistatic ISAR imaging using FMCW radar under the model of Bistatic radar systems. Firstly, the echo signal of FMCW radar which in Bistatic system is analyzed, the coupling terms of range fast time and azimuth slow time which including uniquely in FMCW signal are extracted from the phase of echo signal; then its forms in range Doppler domain and influences to range profile are analyzed; Simultaneously the corresponding compensation algorithm is applied to compensate the coupling terms. The last simulations show that the proposed compensation algorithm in this paper improves the defocus phenomenon which caused by using FMJCW signal and can achieve good imaging of targets.

articleTitle: A new dual frequency band antenna for indoor GSM/UMTS/WLAN applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the prototype of a fork shaped antenna working in dual different frequency bands and suitable to be utilized for indoor applications is described. It can operate at GSM/UMTS/WLAN frequency bands. The physical size of the antenna is 100×100×50 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed antenna is assessed by means of both simulations and measurements.

articleTitle: Design and application of rectangular spiral EBG
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, we investigate effects of several design parameters, including turn number and unit cell size, on the stopband performance of rectangular spiral EBG structure by HFSS. The results of conventional EBG structure and rectangular spiral EBG structure are compared. In addition, the spiral EBG structure is applied into microstrip antenna. It is demonstrated that gain and FBR are improved.
