articleTitle: Analysis of forward scattering properties of rectangular beams in metal space frame radomes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the concept of forward scattering cross section (SCS) is proposed to predict the forward scattering of rectangular beams because the classical induced field ratio (IFR) theory isn't completely appropriate for analysing forward scattering properties of metal beams in metal space frame radomes. The combined field integral equation and moments method are used to deduce and analyse the forward scattering cross section of three-dimensional rectangular beams. The forward scattering properties of metal beams in different parameters are stimulated over broad frequency bands using moments method in conjunction with the asymptotic waveform evaluation technique. Lastly, the results are validated by CST simulation and measurement, which will support the design of metal space frame radomes theoretically.

articleTitle: An algorithm combined with EOFs analysis and MART for GPS-based ionospheric tomography
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Ionospheric imaging usually involves solving an underdetermined inversion problem. The inversion involving additional constraints is performed to enforce realistic profiles in the vertical. A new algorithm combined with empirical orthonormal functions (EOFs) analysis and multiplicative algebraic reconstruction technique (MART) for GPS-based ionospheric tomography has been given in this paper. EOFs can be used to reconstruct the background ionospheric electron density effectively with lower distortion, while the MART can lead to more accuracy by iteration. Numerical simulations and its application on actual GPS-based TEC observations proved that this algorithm offers better performance in physical study of the anomaly, particularly under storm events when its morphology deviates from normal.

articleTitle: An improved PGA algorithm for ionosphere phase perturbation correction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Ionosphere phase perturbation destroys the coherence of echo signal for sky-wave Over-The-Horizon Radar (OTHR) and broadens the spectrum of signal and clutter, which will exacerbate the property of low-speed object detection. PGA (Phase Gradient Autofocus) is an excellent perturbation correction algorithm with properties of logical, concise, robust etc for various perturbations. In particularly, it will reduce computation work enormously. However, the estimate accuracy of PGA is degraded when the Bragg peak filter bandwidth is selected improperly, or the zero frequency components are not acquired exactly, then the iteration times should be increased. An improved PGA is proposed for ionosphere phase perturbation correction, which can realize adaptive selection of the first order clutter filter bandwidth. At the same time, a method of zero frequency abstraction based on Bragg frequencies symmetry is presented, which can decrease iteration times with same perturbation function estimate accuracy and higher computation efficiency.

articleTitle: HTc rf SQUID magnetometer as low frequency antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Antenna is a key component of radio system. The existing low-frequency (refering to 3Hz-30KHz) receiving antenna has low efficiency, high level noise, and low sensitivity. We propose using HTc rf SQUID magnetometer as low frequency receiving antenna to improve the receiving system's performance. Therefore, we introduce a typical low-frequency radio system to demonstrate the effectiveness of HTc rf SQUID antenna.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband SSN suppression using novel electromagnetic band-gap structures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel EBG structure with wideband suppression of the simultaneous switching noise (SSN) in high-speed printed circuit board. Meander lines, which are inserted into the patch, are used to increase the effective inductance of EBG patches. The novel design proposed here is validated numerically, the simulated results show the -30 dB suppression bandwidth ranges from 270 MHz to 15 GHz. The novel design are compared with the AI-EBG of the same parameters, the bandwidth is increased by about 346%, and the lower cut-off frequency is decreased by 830 MHZ. Good signal integrity performance can be obtained by using differential transmission lines.

articleTitle: Synthesis of linear array with broad nulls using immune algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: An improved immune algorithm (IA) is proposed for pattern synthesis of linear antenna array with broad nulls steering. Gauss mutation and adaptive clonal scale control methods are presented to increase the antibodies' diversity and enhance the global searching performance. In this paper, excitation amplitude of the array is setted as antibodies using realcode for steering broad nulls with specified width and at specified direction. Well simulatied results show the fine validity of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of optimal and reduced-dimension STAP for airborne phased array radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The performance of the optimal and reduced-dimension Space-Time Adaptive Processing (STAP) algorithms for the airborne phased array radar is investigated in this paper. The clutter suppression in the mainbeam and the sidelobe clutter regions and the computation load are analyzed and compared between the optimal and two kinds of typical reduced-dimension STAP algorithms, i.e. the 2-D temporal-spatial adaptive algorithm (TSA) and the m-bins Doppler transform-space adaptive processing (mDT-SAP) algorithm. Based on the performance analysis of these STAP algorithms, a new clutter suppression strategy is proposed with consideration of actual clutter environment and the spatial channel and temporal pulse restricted system, which can detect the target more effectively and implement more easily for the airborne phased array radar.

articleTitle: A novel broadband reflectarray antenna using windmill elements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A novel centre-fed printed reflectarray using windmill elements is presented. The analysis of the structure and computation of the phase curves for the field reflected from the patches, needed for the design of the elements, have been carried out with the commercial software Ansoft HFSS. The reflectarray sample is a 37-elements structure, and the results have shown good pattern behaviour and symmetry. The highest measured gain is about 18 dBi with 1 dBi drop within 22% bandwidth at the centre frequency of 10 GHz.

articleTitle: Availability analysis of GSM network systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The Global System for Mobile communication (GSM) is now worldwide-accepted standard for digital cellular systems. With the increasing of GSM popularity, customers are expecting a high level of service, from which availability is considered the major measure of quality. The availability block diagram model is selected to model the system, taking into account the signal strength and signal covering overlaps exist in GSM systems. The real data is collected from Korek telecom. The results show that overlapping cells ensure that full coverage retained, even in the case of hardware outage. The main problem can be concluded after analyses the statistics of different components of RBS is high value of MTTR of CDU's, Antenna System and DRU's, which cause the lowest availability value compare to the other components. Increasing number of Microwaves HOPs, decrease the overall availability and reliability of the cellular system. It is the first time the availability of GSM network performance is studied with real data on ground and functioning.

articleTitle: Design of a simple and compact monopole UWB antenna with controllable band-notched function
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A compact planar monopole antenna with standard band-notched characteristic suitable for ultra-wideband (UWB) applications is presented. This microstrip-fed antenna, consisting of a bevelled and slotted rectangular planar monopole with a vertical tuning stub, only occupies a small size of 30(W)×35(L) ×1.6(H) mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> included the ground plane. The length and width of the stub primarily determine the notched frequency of the antenna and thus a controllable band-notched function is achieved. To improve the impedance bandwidth for UWB applications, a bevelled ground plane is used too. Compared to other designs, the antenna has a quite simple structure to achieve the band-notched characteristic to reduce the effect caused by the frequency interference. Measured results show good agreement with the simulated results and the proposed antenna has an impedance bandwidth of 2.8-13.90 GHz for a voltage standing-wave ratio less than 2, except frequency notched band of 4.8-5.6 GHz. Furthermore, good Omni directional radiation patterns indicate that the proposed antenna is well suited to be integrated within various portable devices for UWB application.

articleTitle: Analysis for phase center of Pyramidal horn antennas for out of band
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The idea of this paper roots in the electromagnetic compatibility design of the whole aircraft system, in which out of band characteristics of airborne antennas are of equal importance as their characteristics in band. The definition of antenna characteristics for out of band is interpreted. Pyramidal horn antennas are the main research objects in this paper and focus on analyzing and investigating phase center features for out of band. The characterization framework of horn antennas phase center for out of band is established, and the theoretical expressions of their phase center for out of band are given. In ensuring better antenna characteristics in band, phase centers of two pyramidal horn antennas out of band and in band that are different types of sizes, different frequency band width are simulated and analyzed by using the integrated analysis method about electromagnetic simulation software combined with the theoretical calculation, and adopting a variance minimization method in statistical data processing. It is meaningful to analyze and summarize the different characteristics of equivalent phase center for these pyramidal horn antennas in band and out of band. The results show that: phase center of pyramidal horn antennas is the law within the working frequency band and out of working band, and this change characteristics affects radiation pattern characteristics of pyramidal horn antennas.

articleTitle: Effect of apertures on the speckle size from rough surfaces
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Based on the scattering theory from rough surfaces and Gaussian moment theorem, the relationship between the apertures and the three-dimensional size of the speckle in the far field are discussed. The results show that the three-dimensional dimension of the speckle is closely dependent on the shape of and the size of the apertures. The lateral speckle size is positive proportional to the ratio of the wavelength and the distance to the size of the apertures, while the longitudinal speckle size is positive proportional to the wavelength and the square of the ratio of the distance to the size of the aperture size. The different the shape of the aperture, the different the proportion factor.

articleTitle: Propagation of 0.1∼0.8THz waves in sand-dust
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Propagation of THz waves from 0.1THz to 0.8THz in sand-dust are studied using Mie theory and Monte Carlo(MC) simulation. Scattering characteristics of a spherical sand-dust particle illuminated by THz waves are analyzed by Mie theory. The extinction efficiency factor, the asymmetry parameter and scattering intensity versus frequency of incident waves are computed. With MC algorithm, the reflectivity, transmittance and backscattering intensity of a THz wave in sand-dust layers is simulated.

articleTitle: Novel wavy EBG structures for ultra-wideband ground bounce noise suppression
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Two novel wavy electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structures have been proposed and applied to power/ground plane pairs for ultra-wideband ground bounce noise (GBN) suppression. The proposed two designs have shown good performance. The -40 dB suppression bandwidth of the first design is from 344 MHz to 20 GHz. For the second design, the -49 dB suppression bandwidth is from 304 MHz to 20 GHz. Both results of simulation and measurement are presented to verify the performance.

articleTitle: Novel ultrawide-band omnidirectional circular disk monopole antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The ultrawide-band antenna is one of the hot research areas. Based on the conventional ultrawide-band circular disk monopole antenna, a novel miniaturized ultrawide-band monopole antenna is presented in this paper. The simulation results demonstrate that the antenna can work well in the 2.3GHz∼24GHz frequency range. Compared with the conventional antenna, the novel antenna has better omnidirection in H-plane radiation pattern. It is proposed to be used in mobile communication and satellite communication with good prospects.

articleTitle: Frequency response from one-dimensional rough surface with the pulsed wave excitation by the FDTD method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A frequency response of one-dimensional (1-D) randomly rough surface in the far zone is investigated by the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithm. A FDTD calculation is performed with a pulse wave excitation, and the representative time-domain scattered field in the far zone is obtained directly by extrapolating the currently calculated data on the output boundary. Then the frequency response of 1-D rough surface is acquired by transforming the representative time-domain field to the frequency domain by a Fourier transform, corrected with a simple multiplicative factor. The normalized radar cross section versus frequency from 1-D rough surface with Gaussian spectrum and PM sea spectrum is compared with the result by FDTD with the sinusoidal wave illumination, which requires an individual FDTD run for every frequency. Finally, the frequency response of rough surface and the representative scattered field in the far zone versus time are analyzed in detail.

articleTitle: Design of an ultra-wideband antenna with dual band-notched characteristic
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband antenna with dual band-notched characteristic is designed. The antenna is based on the rectangle planar monopole antenna. By modifying the radiation patch to octagon and insetting a concave in the ground, the antenna has a good impedance match over a broad frequency range. With two T-shaped slots being cut from the octagonal patch, the dual band-notched characteristic is achieved. The measured and simulated results showed that the antenna has a good performance with VSWR<;2 in the band range from 3.1GHz to 10.6GHz except the bandwidths around 3.5GHz and 5.8GHz. Furthermore, the novel antenna presents a good radiation pattern. Thus, it's suitable for short distance wireless communication inside.

articleTitle: Study of water-injected pork and pork freshness using microwave techniques
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Meat quality and its detection is very important to the improvement of people's life level, especially, nondestructive testing techniques to detect meat quality are focus to researchers of home and abroad constantly. This paper introduces the measuring method in this field, and then the improvement and new trends of nondestructive testing techniques for quality detection of meat were also summarized. With the development of microwave techniques, it has been used widely in the detection of food quality. In this paper a methodology for testing the quality of pork using microwave techniques is presented. By observing the effect of injecting water into pork and the process of putrefaction of pork, the measured S21 of pork samples exhibit certain variation trend and can be used to inspect its quality. This technique can be further developed for commercial purpose and has good prospect in the future.

articleTitle: Effect of different structural parameters on Bandwidth and Resonant frequency of Novel MTM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper utilizes the effect of different structural parameters on Bandwidth and Resonant frequency of Novel planar metamaterial (MTM) structure. This proposed MTM structure shows lower resonant frequency than already designed UCPBG structure. Reflection phase characteristics of unit cell of this MTM structure are simulated using the Ansoft's HFSS software to observe resonance frequencies and also effect of different structure parameters on band width of planar MTM are studied. As we decreases the size of patches the resonant frequency as well as band width increases. As substrate thickness increases which leads to increase in bandwidth. For 0.08 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7GHz</sub> substrate thickness the band width is nearly 1GHz. This planar MTM structure covers a wide band gap of 3.5 GHz which is useful for applications working in X-band of frequency range.

articleTitle: Analysis of periodic structures using FDTD method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The use of FDTD method is a popular technique employed in periodic structure simulations. This paper examines the implementation of split-filed FDTD and Spectral FDTD methods. While following distinctive schemes, both methods exhibit good accuracy in the results. Then based on the resource consumption and speed behaviour during the simulation, it is concluded that these two methods are suitable for different occasions depending on the problem type and computing platform.

articleTitle: An EMC optimized design method of printed circuit board
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents the analysis and study of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) design and optimize process. Take a new electronic product for example, the method is used synchronously. Through simulation and forecast the EMC of electronic product, find the EMC problem in design. Then, an optimizing design method is proposed based on the theory of resonance effect, the result shows that the method is effective.

articleTitle: Design of image-reject hairpin filter applied for Ku-band LNB
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: An image-reject hairpin bandpass filter used in Ku-band low noise block (LNB) is designed, and optimized in the paper. The designed detail of the filter is explained and the image-reject is illustrated theoretically. According to the research, under the condition of reducing the size as small as possible, the hairpin filter used in Ku-band LNB we designed not only can satisfy the demands from bandwidth and return loss, but also has good image-reject. In the end, the results of the simulation and measurement are presented, which prove the feasibility of our design.

articleTitle: Influences of high voltage wires on far-field antenna measurement
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Surrounding environment is one of the main factors which significantly affect the far-field antenna measurement system. To analyze the influences of high voltage wires on far-field antenna measurement, a method is provided that the amplitude and phase of transmission data are compared whether there are high voltage wires beside the antenna measurement field or not. The analysis method and the simulation results are given in this paper.

articleTitle: Tag antennas using differentially connected UC-PBG elements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A tag antenna mountable on a metallic surface is investigated. The tag size is 10.08cm by 4.9cm. Two compact photonic band gap (UCPBG) elements with a ground plane are differentially connected as a radiating unit. By this way, high impedance surface may be realized. While using a larger conductor ground plane, the reader range is around 1.6m.

articleTitle: Research on six-degree-of-freedom electromagnetic tracking system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the model of six-degree-of-freedom electromagnetic tracking system is introduced. To promote the precision and stability of calculating an object's parameters, a new improved arithmetic is presented, which is a combination of the maximal ponderance of unit pointing vector tracking arithmetic and the eigenvector arithmetic. The correction is validated by the numerical simulation results. In the design of circuits, the technologies of direct digital synthesis (DDS), complex programmable logic device (CPLD), digital signal processing (DSP) and so on is introduced, which realize the functions of high-quality sine signal generator, precise sequential control, high-speed data collection and process, and improve the precision of the system.

articleTitle: Localization of Lee model based on measured data
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This article analyzes radiowave propagation prediction model of Lee thoroughly, and limitation is presented using this method; mathematical basis of model localization is given, and a high-accuracy radiowave propagation prediction model is obtained after model localization; the article shows that the error of new Lee model can be controlled in less than 20%.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering of a uniaxial anisotropic sphere to a circular polarization wave
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Electromagnetic scattering of a plane wave with circular polarization from a uniaxial anisotropic sphere with arbitrary primary optical axis is researched. The incident circular polarization wave is expanded in terms of the spherical vector wave functions (SVWF's) in arbitrary primary optical axis coordinate and the expansion coefficients are derived by superposition of the expansion coefficients of two linear polarization waves. The electromagnetic fields in the uniaxial anisotropic sphere are proposed in the integrating forms of the spherical vector wave functions by introducing the Fourier transform. Utilizing the continuous tangential boundary conditions, both of the scattered and internal field coefficients are analytically derived. Scattering property of a uniaxial anisotropic sphere to a circular polarization wave is numerically analyzed and compared with that to a linear polarization wave. The effects of the anisotropy and different primary optical axis on scattering performance are also studied.

articleTitle: Design of circular patch antennas for bluetooth, HIPERLAN, and X band (8.4 GHz) applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents a design of a multiband microstrip circular patch antenna. The antenna of a single patch is designed for the operation at 2.45 GHz and 5.2 GHz ISM (industrial, scientific, and medical) band. This band is occupied by the bluetooth and high performance radio local area network (HIPERLAN) applications. In addition, with the aid of a circular array, the previous antenna can be designed to operate in a place of x band (8.4 GHZ) used by the spacecraft-to-ground communication link. The return loss, input impedance, and the radiation pattern are calculated. Under the condition of the return loss is less than 10dB, the bandwidth at 2.45, 5.2 and 8.4 GHz are 24%, 7.7%, and 6.7%, respectively. The analysis and design of the antenna is carried out using of the finite difference time domain (FDTD) with the perfect matched layer (PML) in addition to a numerical package based on the method of moment (MOM). The obtained results are compared with the available published data and the results of the cavity resonance technique. Good agreements are found.

articleTitle: Scattering matrix method for the optimized design of 0.22 THz corrugated circular waveguide mode converter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Different from the traditional method of solving coupled-mode equations to analyze 0.22 THz gyrotron circular waveguide TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0n</inf>-TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode conversion, the scattering matrix method based on the conservation of complex power technique (CCPT) is introduced to give full-wave analysis for optimal design of the converter. The numerical result is in agreement with that of HFSS simulation. The mode converter designed using this method can achieve efficiencies above 98.65%, bandwidth exceeding 7.8 GHz and 14.1 GHz respectively.

articleTitle: The SP-FDTD method for high-order FDTD plane wave injection
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In the paper, the method of splitting plane wave FDTD (SP-FDTD) algorithm, an efficient method of introducing plane wave source into finite difference time domain grids, is presented for solving oblique incident wave for the modified high-order FDTD (M24 scheme). Numerical examples in 2-D demonstrate the valid of the method and normalized field leakage was measured at -320 dB levels.

articleTitle: An acceleration technique for 2D Ray Tracing simulation based on the research of diffraction in urban environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Despite their good performance, the widespread diffusion of Ray Tracing field-prediction models is still limited due to their high complexity and high computation time. In this paper, a novel method for efficient computation of complex channel characteristics due to multipath effects in urban microcell environments is proposed, aimed at reducing the number of ray-building intersection tests to be handled by the algorithm. With the proposed method, a great computation time reduction can be achieved without sensibly affecting the accuracy of the prediction.

articleTitle: A behavioral quantification analytical method of electromagnetic susceptibility at board level
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents the behavioral quantification analytical method of electromagnetic susceptibility (EMS) for electronic devices at board level. A full-wave electromagnetic modeling technique coupled with a circuit-based method is used in this paper to quantitatively describe the interference immunity of sensitive components in the circuit board. The behavioral model for quantitative analysis of electromagnetic susceptibility is established. Hence, the prior design of electromagnetic susceptibility at board level can be achieved.

articleTitle: The passband characteristics of Composite Right/Left-handed Transmission Line with finite number of cells
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A closed form of S21 is deduced to analyze the passband characteristic of Composite Right/Left-handed Transmission Line (CRLH TL) using the eigenvalue decomposition and network parameter method. The passband characteristics versus the number of cells has been analyzed and illustrated. This method will be more precise than Bloch algorithm when N < 10, and the increase in the number of cells N will improve the band-pass filtering performance effectively.

articleTitle: Effects of objective functions on evaporation duct height estimation from radar sea clutter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A new evaporation duct profile structure is presented by two parameters: evaporation duct height and strength. Two different objective functions are also introduced and analyzed, which show that the objective functions are multi-peak and not sensitive to evaporation duct strength. Based on the new duct model and the two objective functions, the estimations are operated by using differential evolutionary (DE) algorithm. All the estimated results are obtained by 200 Monte Carlo simulations and statistically analyzed. The effects of population size (PS) and clutter to noise ratio (CNR) is also investigated. The analyzed results show that increasing PS can not effectively improve the accuracy of estimations. However, high CNR can obviously improve the accuracy.

articleTitle: Application of AWE to scattering analysis of the double-negative medium
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The PMCHWT equation of the double negative media (DNG) is obtained based on its constitutive relationship. And the surface currents and radar cross section (RCS) at a single frequency point is computed by Method of moments (MOM). The asymptotic waveform evaluation (AWE) technique for dispersive dielectric medium is deduced and applied to electromagnetic scattering analysis of double-negative medium within a given frequency hand.

articleTitle: Mismatching design method for RFID tag antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents an original design method (mismatching design method) for RFID tag antenna application through the analysis of the Radar Cross Section (RCS) in RFID system. This design method can achieve the largest delta RCS than traditional way so that it optimizes the stability of the RFID system. The Thevenin equivalent circuit model of the tag antenna is discussed which displays the limit of the mismatching design method. Finally, a design example is given by using the method presented and the result verifies the validity of the analysis in this paper.

articleTitle: A novel approach to analysing RCS of the airborne antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Currently, the parameter characterizing scattering performance of airborne antenna is still the free space radar cross section (free space RCS). However, without considering the coupling between antennas and the plane, this parameter does not adequately reflect the effects how the antenna affects the plane's RCS after installation. To solve this problem, this article researches the coupling effects of the scattering fields in between. Then a new simulation program is designed to achieve the simulation of the antenna's airborne radar cross section (airborne RCS). And the total RCS of both is achieved by two models and compared with the default results. Model one: synthesizing the antenna's airborne RCS and the plane's RCS; model two: synthesizing the antenna's free space RCS and the plane's RCS. The results show that the curve achieved from the new synthesis model is closer to the default total RCS curve. This suggests that the airborne RCS is better to reflect the characteristics of the antenna scattering performance after installation. Actual project may adopt the simulation program in this paper to predict the antenna RCS before installation. If it does so, it will save costs and shorten design cycles greatly.

articleTitle: Measurement of energy absorption flux during ionospheric heating in polar region
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Based on energy and momentum equations, the energy absorption flux near the reflection height is calculated by using the electron density, electron temperature and ion temperature measured in the heating campaign on August 16-19 2009. It is shown that the energy absorption flux is close to Gauss distribution, but the structure is not symmetric along beam absorption centre. The curve of absorption maximum with frequency difference exists break point near 0.6MHz, and we can carry out an optimization heating in a critical state, which is important for building the experiential and semi-experiential model of energy absorption flux.

articleTitle: Transient analytic solutions of lossless multiconductor transmission line excited by plane-wave
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: An analytic method is used to calculate the transient responses of the lossless multiconductor transmission line. The frequency-domain responses of lossless multiconductor transmission line excited by plane-wave are calculated by the frequency-domain Baum-Liu-Tesche (BLT) equation. By expressing the BLT equation in a matrix series, an analytical transformation from the frequency domain to the time-domain is performed to obtain the transient response. The simulation results are in good agreement with the results obtained by using the frequency-domain BLT equation via an inverse fast Fourier transform.

articleTitle: Dual-band bandpass filter using stub loaded resonators with multiple transmission zeros
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A dual-band bandpass filter using both an open stub-loaded resonator (OSLR) and a short stub-loaded resonator (SSLR) is presented. The use of SSLR has the advantage that a transmission zero can be flexibly controlled by tuning the length of the short stub, which can be employed as a new but convenient way to create transmission zeros in front of passbands in filter design. By further introducing a two-order planar transversal filter structure using the OSLR as well as the source-load coupling, a dual-band filter is implemented with four transmission zeros and exhibits high skirt selectivity based on the simulated result. Two passbands with center frequencies of 2.45 GHz and 3.5 GHz are achieved with compact size of about 0.18λ × 0.12λ at 2.45 GHz.

articleTitle: Rayleigh scattering property of an anisotropic medium particle
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The finite difference equation is developed, which may be used to calculate the electric field of the inhomogeneous anisotropic medium. The validity of the equation is tested. The distributions of the electric potential and the electric field are presented for an anisotropic trihedron body. Its Rayleigh scattering property is researched. Simulations show that the dielectric constant in the polarizing direction of the incident electric field has an obvious impact on scattering, the dielectric constant in the perpendicular direction has not much effect on it. The arithmetic is not confined by the factors such as the target's shape and electric parameter etc. and has the peculiarities of briefness and versatility.

articleTitle: The application of CPML in analysis of the characteristic of EMP propagation in crooked tunnel
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method has been applied to analyze the characteristic of EMP propagation in tunnel, which can be seen as a waveguide approximately, and is excited by propagation model such as TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>, TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>, etc. In order to improve the effectiveness of the absorbing boundary condition, a perfectly matched layer (PML) medium with complex frequency-shifted (CFS) constitutive parameters is introduced for this study. The absorbing boundary is implemented by using the convolution PML (CPML), and the absorbing efficiency of CPML is compared with traditional PML. Numerical results show that the CPML provides for a more efficient absorbing boundary than that of the traditional PML at absorbing evanescent modes, and consequently the computation domain and computation time can be greatly reduced.

articleTitle: Synthesis of a plane wave in the near field using genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The synthesis of a plane wave is a key problem in near-field antenna measurements or near-field scattering measurements. The genetic algorithm is introduced and applied in the plane wave synthesis technique. with the linear array made up of infinitely long current filaments as the theoretical model of plane wave synthesis and the results are compared with that obtained by the Least Square method. The calculation results show that the uniform degree of the amplitude and phase of the quasi-plane wave synthesized in the body under test zone are improved illustrates the advantages of the genetic algorithm over the Least Square method.

articleTitle: Forecasting the ionospheric foF2 in Chinese region by neural network technique
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: By using artificial neural network (NN) and considering the effects of the solar and geomagnetic activities on the ionosphere, a method for forecasting the ionospheric critical frequency, f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, up to 5 hour ahead at any target geographic location in Chinese region has been proposed. The inputs of the NN are time, day of the year, geographical latitude, solar zenith angle, the twelve recent past observations of f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and the 30-day mean moving values of f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> from the target location. The outputs of the NN are F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+1</sub>, F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+2</sub>, F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+3</sub>, F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+4</sub>, F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+5</sub>, representing the values of f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> up to 5h ahead. Data from Wulumqi, Changchun, Chongqing and Guangzhou stations spanning the period 1958-1968 are used for training the NN. Historical data at nine different stations in China are used to checkout the network respectively (Not including the training set). The performance of the NN is measured by calculating the root-mean-square error (RMS) difference between the NN outputs and measured station data. The results indicate that the prediction of NN has good agreement with measured data.

articleTitle: Analysis of the influence of soil resistivity on lightning radiation magnetic field
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The lightning radiation field propagating above lossy ground, which may be modified by the propagation effect of soil resistivity, is investigated. Based on the expression of the radiation field from dipole, the effect of soil resistivity on lightning radiation field is analyzed in both time and frequency domain. It is indicated that, compared with the case of perfect ground conductor, the resistivity of soil causes decrease in the magnitude and increase in the rise time of lightning radiation magnetic field. Changes in the peak value and derivative of the corresponding inverted lightning current are also investigated.

articleTitle: Design & measurement techniques for Dual Polarized Novel Printed Crossed Slot Dipole Antenna for Remote Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper discusses the design & measurement techniques for Dual Polarized Novel Printed Crossed Slot Dipole Antenna for Remote Sensing Applications. An innovative dual polarized antenna has been designed which consists both polarizations i.e. linear & circular polarization achieved through two independent electronic phase shifters providing phase shifts of 0° & 90° at both inputs for circular polarization & phase shifts of 0° & 0° at both inputs for linear polarization, however equal power at both inputs is provided through Wilkinson power divider. Antenna has wide beamwidth characteristics of 100° for providing global coverage required for remote sensing application. Due to wide coverage of the antenna the link can be easily established regardless of the position of the satellite. Peak Circularly polarized gain of 6.85 dB has been achieved through excitation of both feeding ports & linearly polarized gain of 7.35 dB has been achieved with excitation of both ports. This novel design overcomes the limitation of normal patch antenna configurations which provide only one type of polarization in one design by providing both polarizations in one design. Printed Slot crossed dipole antenna provides bandwidth of 200MHz which is sufficient for our application. Absolute gain measurement techniques have been employed for the measurement of antenna gain. Simulation & Optimization for this novel antenna has been done on Ansoft HFSS v11.

articleTitle: A dual-band tapered slot omni-directional antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A dual-band tapered slot omni-directional antenna with an orthogonal arc-shaped parasitic element which covers GSM/DCS/PCS/CDMA2000/WCDMA/TD-SCDMA/WLAN/ WiMAX is realized experimentally. The proposed antenna consists of two shunted tapered slot antennas. The tapered slot antenna is an asymmetric structure which is made up of a straight line and an exponential line. An arc-shaped parasitic element which improves the radiation pattern effectively is orthogonal with the radiator element. The measured 14-dB impedance bandwidth of the antenna is 29.5% and 54.6% at the lower band and the higher band, respectively. And the measured 10-dB impedance bandwidth is 129.2% (0.69GHz-3.21GHz) centred at 1.95GHz, which is about 45 times that of the corresponding monopolar wire-patch antenna. The proposed antenna is successfully simulated, designed, and measured, showing dual-band impedance bandwidth, stable gain and good omni-directional radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Compressive sensing for wide-angle analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A new incident source with different angles was constructed for dealing with wide-angle scattering problems. Considering the impendence matrix in method of moments (MOM) is independent from incident angles, the equivalent relationship between induced current and the measured CS-current was build, while the CS-current can be computed directly under the new incident source. Finally, we can reconstruct the induce current by utilizing the theory of compressive sensing (CS). Compared with traditional MOM, the computational complexity can be greatly reduced.

articleTitle: A pattern reconfigurable printed quasi-Yagi antenna with slots in the directors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a pattern reconfigurable printed quasi-Yagi antenna with slots in the directors is presented. The simulation results show that the impedance bandwidth of the proposed antenna is excellent, and the gain variation within operating bandwidth is relatively small. By controlling the states of the switches, the main beam of the proposed antenna in the xoy plane can be shifted to the one of four angles. The antenna is also fabricated and measured. There is a good agreement between the simulated and measured results. The proposed antenna has the potential for modern wireless communication.

articleTitle: Analysis of a novel model for dispersive media
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Nowadays the common way for dealing with electromagnetic problems in dispersive media is based on a certain classical model. But it is not accurate enough to set up a general model on the basis of only one approximate model since the natural dispersive media are quite complicated. A piecewise linear composite model is proposed that combines the three general models (i. e., Debye, Lorentz and Drude models). Numerical fitting example for metamaterial proves the correctness and validity of the proposed new model.

articleTitle: An improved array design for the DMUSIC algorithm based on Simulated Annealing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A Simulated Annealing based array design for direction-of-arrival (DOA) is introduced in this paper. Decoherent Multichannel Signal Classification (DMUSIC) algorithm is applied for the design method. Simulations have been made to test the performance of the proposed method. Finally, the summary is made that the method is both efficient and accurate.

articleTitle: A study on the ionospheric parameter f02 instantaneous mapping based on equivalent sunspot number
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A CRI (Chinese Reference Ionosphere model) based kriging real time updating method for f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is presented in this paper. This method uses effective sunspot number ( eff R ) and selects the relative difference between the observed and the CRI model calculated values of f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> as the variable. During solar maximum, the root mean square error is 1.32MHz and the relative error is 14.86%. While during solar minimum, the root mean square error is 1.06 MHz, and the relative error is 19.02%. On average, the globally root mean square error is 1.2MHz, and the globally relative error is 17.07%. The evaluate method of ‘relative comparison method’ is put forward, and by comparing with the algorithm without using R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf>, the root mean square error is reduced by 0.75%,and the relative error is decreased by 1.05%.

articleTitle: An improved design of absorbing structure with Jerusalem cross slot
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a type of thin planar absorbing structure of Jerusalem cross slot (JCS) is presented, which has the virtue of wider bandwidth and broader adjustment range. The absorption frequency band can be flexibly adjusted by the slot parameters. The influences of various structure parameters of JCS, incident wave polarization and variation of incident angles on the absorption characteristics are analyzed to provide guidance on theoretical design for practical application. The validation and effectiveness of the proposed design are conducted by using waveguide simulation and measurement.

articleTitle: On integrated visual optimization system for large reflector antenna structures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Reflector antenna structural design is an integrated problem involving structural and electromagnetic performance analysis. The synthetic analysis is discussed in details of reflector antennas based on the coupled mathematical optimization model of structural-electromagnetic performances. The optimization procedure is developed based on the improvement of both the structural performances and electromagnetic performances. Finally, the coupled analysis platform is developed, which integrates the techniques of the data library management, the selection of optimization algorithm, and variable resolution and merge. An optimization analysis of a 16-m antenna is made by the platform with useful and satisfying result obtained showing the potential of optimization platform.

articleTitle: Estimating low-altitude atmospheric refractivity structure from multi-frequency radar returns
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: An estimation model for atmospheric refractivity structure based on multi-frequency radar sea returns is introduced in this paper. The model was assessed using evaporation duct inversion processes with a two-parameter environmental model employed. Through comparisons of RMS evaporation duct height and strength errors predicted by multi-frequency and single-frequency estimation model, it is illustrated that this multi-frequency model is more robust in atmospheric refractivity structure inversion.

articleTitle: The Pad Printing technology evaluation in mobile phone antenna manufacture
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Diversification, styling, miniaturization and cost reduction are trends in the field of portable electronics. The 3D technology is an innovative way to meet this demand. This paper evaluated the Pad Printing 3D antenna manufacture technology which offers versatile and cost effective interconnection platform compared to the flex-antenna or sheet metal technologies. The basic Pad Printing process was introduced firstly, the printing ink RF parameter including conductivity, skin depth and inductor loss which are important to the antenna performance was analyzed then. An penta-band mobile phone antenna with same radiator pattern was processed using Pad Printing technology and the common flex antenna technology, their s11 and efficiency was compared with each other. Other parameters including the antenna mechanical, environmental and mass production capacity was evaluated lastly. As a result, the Pad Printing manufacture technology have a relatively good potential for antenna mass production application.

articleTitle: Sensitivity enhancement in optical waveguide sensors based on TM wave and metamaterials
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The sensitivity of the optical TM wave waveguide with four-layer was derived in this paper. The variation of the sensitivity of the proposed sensor with different parameters of the waveguide is studied. We verify that the proposed sensor can dramatically enhance the sensitivity compared with the conventional three-layer TM wave waveguide sensors without metamaterials. Moreover, this sensor is more sensitive than optical waveguide sensor based on TE wave.

articleTitle: FDTD investigation on scattering of a plasma-coated target above a rough sea surface
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper the composite scattering from a sea surface and a plasma-coated target is investigated by the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method. Both the sea water and the plasma layer are regarded as the isotropic and dispersive medium, and they satisfy the Debye model and the Drude model, respectively. The auxiliary differential equation (ADE) technique is incorporated into the FDTD scheme to deal with the dispersive medium. The frequency response of composite model is computed for the different polarization. The result shows that the radar cross section (RCS) of a plasma-coated target above a sea surface is reduced obviously.

articleTitle: Fast RCS computation over a frequency band based on general asymptotic waveform evaluation: Geometric modelling by NURBS surface
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: To fast calculate the radar cross section (RCS) of an arbitrarily shaped three-dimensional (3D) perfect electric conductor (PEC) body over a frequency band, the method of moments (MOM) in conjunction with the general asymptotic waveform evaluation (GAWE) is applied in this paper. And the 3D body is modelled by the non-uniform rational B-spline (NURBS) surface through the compute aided geometric design (CAGD). Numerical simulations of a square plate and a sphere are shown. Good agreements between the GAWE and the exact solutions obtained by MOM are illustrated. And the GAWE is more effective in computing the RCS over a frequency band. It is necessary to note that the MOM in conjunction with the GAWE technique can be also applied to predict the mono-static RCS of an arbitrarily shaped 3D PEC body.

articleTitle: Real time STD calculation at low elevation by GPS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Global Positioning System (GPS) has become a powerful tool in a number of applications such as the geophysics and remote sensing. Real time slant path tropospheric delay (STD) is of benefit in near real time weather forecasting, climatologic applications, and reconstructing refractivity profile. A new method of acquiring real time STD at very low elevation (0°-5°), is presented in the paper which is based on singular ground-based GPS observations with International GPS Service (IGS) ultra-rapid product. An experiment was carried out to validate the feasibility on an island in Shantou, south China during July 2009. Results from radiosondes, GPS and mapping functions are compared. It shows that the mean error of GPS-derived STD is smaller than mapping function. Consequently, it should be feasible to obtain real time STD at low elevation (0°-5°) by GPS.

articleTitle: TIDs in ionospheric F-region at Cusp latitude: Observations and numerical simulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Travelling Ionospheric Disturbances (TIDs) at Cusp latitude observed by EISCAT-Svalbard radar (ESR) were presented in this paper. Several representative cases were reported in detail, including a case of TIDs appearing at a broad altitude range (up to the topside of ionospheric F-region). Height profiles of wave number k were obtained in F-region using Maximum Entropy spectral Estimation (MESE) method when TIDs were monitored by various radar beams simultaneously. Simulation results indicated that TIDs observed at cusp latitude could be reasonable reproduced by carefully selecting AGW inputs.

articleTitle: Diurnal variation in a long distance VHF tropospheric path in the Brazilian Amazon region
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper deals with an experimental study carried out in a long distance VHF tropospheric path located in the Brazilian Amazon region. Measurements of the received power in this path were registered for 170 hours and clearly indicate a diurnal variation characterized by the existence of two propagation mechanisms. Scatter propagation during the day and diffraction propagation in night hours. This information, together with the knowledge of the median values of the earth k-factor derived from these measurements are important input data for planning VHF and possibly UHF radio systems in low latitude areas.

articleTitle: Signal integrity for high speed digital design
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In an era of compact design and higher clock speed signal integrity is an ever increasing concern for high speed digital design. For any high speed design it is very important to do the signal integrity analysis. In this paper the importance, measurement technique and simulation tools of signal integrity for high speed digital design has been presented in a short and simple way.

articleTitle: Characteristic researches on receiving antenna of coal-rock electromagnetic emission
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Direction characteristic of loop antenna of coal-rock electromagnetic emission is simulated by HFSS software. By comparing the antenna with the metal reflecting flat with the one without the reflecting flat, the research results show that, the signals received by the antenna without the reflecting flat are affected by signals from its back; the gain and direction characteristic of the antenna with the reflecting flat will be improved because signals energy can be controlled to one side. The research can provide foundations for improving the receiving sensitivity of electromagnetic emission and the accuracy of forecasting accuracy of coal-rock disasters.
